title: NVIDIA and Microsoft Expand Accelerated Computing From Azure to Windows PCs
body: NVIDIA and Microsoft Expand Accelerated Computing From Azure to Windows PCs NVIDIA and Microsoft expand tools for enterprises to customize AI models and deploy applications across cloud and local infrastructure. November 19, 2026 by Dave Salvator 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA and Microsoft are extending their full-stack collaboration to help organizations build, customize and deploy intelligent applications — from next-generation infrastructure on Azure to industrial systems and Windows PCs. At Microsoft Ignite , the companies are expanding access to Azure virtual machines powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, as well as adding customer availability to NVIDIA open models and customization capabilities through Microsoft Foundry, and new options for running AI at the edge, where businesses generate and use their data. Microsoft is also using NVIDIA technologies to accelerate its own models and services, including NVIDIA Dynamo inference software for post-training and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs for Bing search models. NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Running in Azure NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are running in Azure data centers , providing infrastructure designed for demanding reasoning, agentic applications, and large-scale model training and inference. Microsoft and NVIDIA are also collaborating to extend confidential computing to bare-metal and rack-scale AI infrastructure. The work will help protect sensitive models and data while they are being processed, supporting organizations that need to work with proprietary or regulated information. NVIDIA Confidential Computing and attestation help customers verify the computing environment before releasing sensitive models, data or keys. As AI workloads span more interconnected accelerators, the companies are working to extend those protections across the AI factory infrastructure. To help data centers get more performance from available power, NVIDIA and Microsoft are also collaborating on power efficiency using NVIDIA MaxLPS . Azure’s Vera Rubin preview builds on NVIDIA and Microsoft’s codesign and performance optimization, underscored in the latest NVIDIA Blackwell-based MLPerf results. In MLPerf Training v6.1 , Azure scaled to 10,240 NVIDIA GPUs with GB200 NVL72 systems on the DeepSeek-V3 model, the largest scale in the round. In MLPerf Inference v6.1 , Azure’s NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems led cloud submissions on DeepSeek-R1 interactive throughput by over 10%, per Signal65. Helping Enterprises Customize and Deploy Open Models Enterprise AI agents need to reason through complex tasks, find relevant company information and understand business documents. NVIDIA and Microsoft are expanding the models and services available through Microsoft Foundry to help developers bring these capabilities into business applications. Microsoft’s serverless Programmed Training offering gives developers control over post-training workflows while Foundry manages the underlying infrastructure. Enterprises can focus on their business data, evaluating model responses and improving model behavior. Foundry Managed Compute adds support for deploying custom model weights, helping connect model customization with deployment through Microsoft’s managed services. EY used Programmed Training in Microsoft Foundry to adapt NVIDIA Nemotron open models for classifying corporate purchasing records, improving accuracy on its evaluation dataset by 55% and lowering cost by 15x compared with proprietary frontier models. The work demonstrates how enterprises can customize open models for specialized business tasks. The expanded NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 lineup on Foundry Managed Compute supports different requirements across enterprise applications. Nemotron 3.5 Super is designed for long-running agents working across coding, research and business workflows, while Lightning supports applications that need fast responses and tool use. Complementary models help agents find relevant information with Nemotron Embed and Rerank, extract structured information from documents with Nemotron Parse and detect harmful content with Nemotron Content Safety. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt — designed for high-throughput, low-latency reasoning — and Transcribe, for speech recognition, are coming soon. Bringing AI Closer to Enterprise Data NVIDIA and Microsoft are expanding deployment options beyond the cloud, helping organizations run models and agents closer to their data while maintaining control over their infrastructure and operations. Expanded support for Nemotron 3.5 in Foundry Local brings capabilities for reasoning, coding and tool-using agents to Azure Local environments. Retrieval models help applications find evidence across text, document images, charts and tables. Azure Local will also support NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs from hardware partners, giving organizations additional options for deploying AI on premises. Azure Local is expanding to NVIDIA Jetson Thor and Jetson Orin edge AI platforms to support industrial applications such as machine vision, robotics and autonomous operations. NVIDIA physical AI models, including Cosmos , are also being brought to Foundry Local. On Windows PCs powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark , NVIDIA and Microsoft will showcase local large language model experiences at Ignite, demonstrating how developers can run AI applications directly on devices. For organizations using Cloud PCs, the companies are bringing Direct Stream capabilities to GPU-accelerated Windows 365 Cloud PCs. These capabilities support demanding graphics applications with up to two 4K streams at 60 frames per second and low latency, even over challenging networks. A limited preview is open for sign-ups, with public preview planned for early 2027. Connecting Scientific AI With Microsoft Discovery For scientific research, NVIDIA BioNemo Agent Toolkit and NVIDIA ALCHEMI Toolkit are expanding into the Microsoft Discovery catalog , bringing models for life sciences, drug discovery and materials and chemical science into Microsoft’s agentic research platform. BioNeMo Agent Toolkit helps scientists use natural language to run computational biology workflows in Microsoft Discovery, with agents coordinating the tools and model calls needed to carry out the work. An initial integration uses the RFD4-Proteina model , developed in collaboration with the University of Washington’s Institute for Protein Design, to generate candidate protein structures and amino acid sequences for further evaluation and laboratory validation. Accelerating Microsoft’s Models and Services Alongside expanding customer access to NVIDIA technologies, Microsoft is using NVIDIA software and accelerated computing in its own AI development and services. Microsoft AI uses NVIDIA Dynamo to support reinforcement learning rollout inference during post-training. This computationally intensive process generates the experiences used to improve models. Dynamo coordinates inference across a large GPU fleet, optimizing performance, as well as helping manage requests, model updates and recovery from failures. The deployment builds on joint engineering between Microsoft AI and NVIDIA. Visit NVIDIA at Ignite for demonstrations spanning enterprise applications, robotics, accelerated data processing and local computing, with hardware including an NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 rack and RTX Spark devices. View NVIDIA sessions, hands-on labs and booth theater presentations . title: How we’re putting one of quantum mechanics’ deepest features to the test at scale.
body: How we’re putting one of quantum mechanics’ deepest features to the test at scale. Nov 19, 2026 Today, in new research published on the cover of Science , Google Quantum AI demonstrated that contextuality — a quantum property scientists believe powers certain quantum algorithms — survives at scale on our quantum processor. What gives quantum computers their unique power? While entanglement usually gets the spotlight, theory suggests that a deeper quantum property called contextuality may power certain quantum algorithms. In simple terms, contextuality means a system’s properties aren’t fixed in advance; what you measure depends on which other compatible measurements you make alongside it. Until recently, this effect had mostly been shown in small systems of just a few particles. Our paper in Science now demonstrates this at scale on our quantum processor. Using it, our qubits won a well-known coordination game 98.3% of the time, beating the 88.9% classical limit, and outperformed constrained classical strategies in tasks spanning up to 105 qubits. These tests also serve as a sensitive new method to catch subtle hardware errors, helping pave the way for real-world applications like chemistry and materials science.

title: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents
body: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents See how developers are combining AI agents with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to build simulation applications, test physical behavior and guide improvements. November 19, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Your browser doesn't support HTML5 video. Here is a link to the video instead. Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem. Physical AI Paves the Path to Autonomous Industrial Operations 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Nyhamna_footage_take5_30s.mp4 AI agents powered by frontier models pave the way to autonomous operations. They use industrial tools and engineering data to help engineers build digital twins that test plans and processes and evaluate operational decisions. Falkor, a KONGSBERG company, shows how this works in practice. The company’s Falkor Surface platform lets customers turn their computer-aided design and engineering data into facility-scale digital twins using the GPT-6 Astra model. The platform uses NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition GPUs on Microsoft Azure to enable advanced physics simulation. AI agents built on Falkor’s agentic engine understand dense technical documentation, spatial relationships and real-world physics. Engineers can create and test plans in simulation before traveling on site, reducing costly delays and mistakes. They can also inspect equipment and check clearances in a shared view. He also used Astra with SimReady ( simready-foundation ) to create the physical scene in simulation. Astra then generated animation and application code to bring those capabilities together. Learn how to prepare and validate SimReady robot assets with frontier AI models and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. Connect an Autonomous-Driving Testing Workflow https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/zero-to-alpamayo-under-10MB.mp4 Changing a scene, sensor or driving model can significantly affect autonomous-vehicle simulations. Doyub Kim, a manager on the simulation technology team at NVIDIA, asked Astra to build Zero to Alpamayo — a reusable simulation environment based on San Francisco’s Market Street. Kim directed Astra to map out the workflow, then connect asset creation, traffic, Omniverse RTX sensor simulation and Alpamayo driving in stages, checking each integration. The resulting prototype was a testing ground for comparing models and tracing how scene or sensor changes affect downstream driving behavior. A separate Cosmos3-Nano experiment varied weather and lighting in recorded simulation videos, allowing Kim to compare the driving model’s responses to the same scenario under different conditions. Use Sensor Differences to Create and Improve Digital Twins https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/0_00-0_004-hubble_rivermark_Real_Sim_no_loop.mp4 Comparing recorded and simulated camera and lidar outputs gives developers key performance indicator-based feedback for refining a scene. To test robots and autonomous vehicles, developers need to know how closely simulated sensors match real ones. Ashley Reid, who works on RTX sensor validation at NVIDIA, directed Astra and Claude Fable 5 agents to compare ovrtx camera and raw LiDAR outputs with recorded data. The agents created two digital twins from scratch and improved two existing ones. Over about three days, Reid guided an iterative workflow in which agents measured differences, created or modified OpenUSD scenes, and checked the results. Changes addressed missing objects, geometry and materials, with acceptance depending on camera and LiDAR metrics. This gives developers a way to use measured discrepancies to guide scene creation and improvement. Start by rendering an OpenUSD scene with the ovrtx minimal Python example , then define a sensor measure to compare with recorded data. Robo Olympics: Test Robot Skills With Simulation Teaching robots new movements means checking whether those actions work under physical constraints. Tae Kim, who leads NVIDIA Omniverse engineering and product, used sports videos and natural-language instructions to guide Astra in building Robo Olympics, an experimental project that tests simulated Unitree G1 humanoids performing sports movements. Under Kim’s direction, Astra built controllers and refined them through physics trials. Newton Physics Engine simulated behavior, the open source NVIDIA Warp framework accelerated calculations and ovrtx rendered scenes and virtual-camera images. In one experiment, the robot cleared a single hurdle in 64 of 100 simulation trials. The trials gave Kim feedback for improving the robot’s timing and control. Watch Kim explore building simulations with Astra and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. Bring the International Space Station Into the Browser Turning 3D models into an application requires connecting assets, live data and an interface. Nic Johns, an engineering director at NVIDIA, prompted Astra to assemble NASA assets into an OpenUSD International Space Station model with telemetry. Johns built the application with a single prompt, then used a follow-up prompt to shift the scene to Earth’s daytime side so the planet was visible. The workflow used Blender for asset preparation and Omniverse libraries for rendering ( ovrtx ), scene runtime (ovstage) and streaming (ovstream). The application brings 3D models and operational data into the browser, with Johns guiding its development through prompts and corrections. Try the Omniverse Real-Time Viewer skill . Turn Captured Rooms Into Testing Environments A digitally reconstructed room needs editable objects and accurate physical behavior before developers can test interactions. Chirag Majithia, from the Isaac engineering applications team at NVIDIA, directed Astra to turn stereo camera captures into an editable OpenUSD studio. The workflow combined PyCuSFM, FoundationStereo and nvblox for reconstruction, with user review guiding object selection and placement. Astra assembled generated and Blender-authored assets and used USD Content Agents to configure how objects move and interact in simulation. Isaac Sim tests guided collision and contact revisions for doors and drawers. The studio connects captured geometry to interaction testing, making gaps and object behavior easier to inspect. Explore USD Content Agents. Have a simulation idea? Explore NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to start building with an AI agent.

title: A smarter way to track and buy clean energy
body: A smarter way to track and buy clean energy Nov 19, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Granular certificates are a next-generation tool to ensure more accurate, impactful clean energy buying. Jenna Stauffer Head of Strategic Priorities, Climate Operations Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Read AI-generated summary We are advancing Granular Certificates to track clean energy by hour and location, providing clear pricing signals that encourage smarter grid management. These tools help you match electricity use with local clean energy production, supporting a more stable power system. You can watch our new video to learn how these certificates help developers, energy asset owners, and the grid. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. We use Granular Certificates to track clean energy supply by specific hour and geographic location. Trading volume in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic region increased 437% during our recent monthly spot auctions. Our support for the Registry Acceleration Fund helps organizations verify and track hourly energy data. These certificates provide new revenue streams for battery storage operators and improve grid stability overall. We reduced our Scope 2 emissions by 3% while managing a 37% increase in electricity load. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. We are using new tools called Granular Certificates to track clean energy by the hour and location. These certificates help us match our electricity use with local solar or wind power, even when the sun is not shining. By creating clear price signals, this system encourages companies to build more batteries and clean energy projects where they are needed most. This helps us manage our power use and supports a cleaner, more stable energy grid. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer Granular Certificates (GCs) are next-generation clean energy instruments. They precisely track supply by hour and location, helping companies match their electricity load with local clean energy. Their hourly pricing signals encourage the development of clean generation and energy storage when and where it is needed most. These instruments can incentivize improved grid management, and they can help accelerate the deployment of advanced clean technologies, leading to a cleaner, more stable power system. But like any nascent solution, the foundational building blocks need to be in place first. We first started piloting GCs in 2021 and, in just five years, they’ve transitioned from early concept to real-world certificates, traded on specific hours. We’re continuing to take actions to accelerate both our own procurement and the global GC ecosystem. Here are three key ways the GC ecosystem advanced this year: 1. The GC marketplace is growing. Marketplaces are critical because they establish transparent hourly pricing signals and help simplify processes for those new to hourly procurement. LevelTen, in partnership with the Granular Certificate Trading Alliance (GCTA) and the Intercontinental Exchange, launched the Granular Certificate Marketplace in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic grid region PJM in October 2025. Since that first auction, trading volume has increased 437% in just one year , with Google participating in every monthly spot auction. This increased trading volume generates clear pricing signals, with higher premiums occurring during evening hours. By demonstrating when buyers need clean energy most, GCs can incentivize suppliers to operate or build clean energy to meet this demand. 2. Global registries help with tracking and verification. Almost every corporate clean energy buyer uses registries, which track and verify their clean energy purchases via instruments like monthly or annual energy attribute certificates (EACs). Registries help also ensure EACs are not double counted, supporting unique clean energy claims. However, until recently, the vast majority of registries didn’t have the technical capabilities to accommodate GCs. To help address those gaps, Google supported the GCTA in establishing the Registry Acceleration Fund . The fund awarded grants to five of the largest organizations that operate registries, which collectively issue or track 4,000 TWh of certificates in over 70+ countries. As of today, one of these organizations has met their technical milestones that would allow them to transfer, verify, and retire GCs. The remaining four organizations are expected to finish in early 2027. This will add critical functionality needed for these instruments to scale, including standardization of the hourly data and traceability to one clear owner. 3. GCs are driving real value. Despite the GC market’s nascency, its potential benefits are moving from academic research concepts towards demonstrating real impact. For example, in a recent GCTA white paper , clean energy developers and asset operators shared real-life perspectives on granular matching. These developers explained that pricing signals from GCs can help them maximize existing energy assets in the near-term, while helping them make crucial decisions about project siting and technology diversification in the longer term. In addition, Google, esVolta, Quintrace, and LevelTen helped prove a new revenue stream for battery energy storage system operators. We partnered to pilot the first GCs for storage systems, shifting solar generation to match our targeted demand hours. This could not have happened without hourly tracking and verification via GCs. Hear more firsthand accounts of the benefits of GCs to developers, energy asset owners, and the grid in our new video . In addition to the maturing global ecosystem, we’ve also continued to evolve our use of GCs to help manage Google’s emissions. We’ll always prioritize applying new, long-term clean energy agreements, and the underlying hourly GCs, first. Even with a large clean energy portfolio, the sun doesn’t always shine and the wind doesn’t always blow exactly when we need it to. Marketplace GCs help fill those gaps. At the same time, our purchases help build a stronger market where GCs can be bought and sold quickly, easily, and in large quantities — creating clearer price signals and providing granular options for growing numbers of buyers. We used a smaller amount of marketplace GCs alongside a much larger amount of clean energy agreements to help lower our Scope 2 market-based emissions by 3% from 2024 to 2025 , despite a 37% electricity load increase. We will include a limited amount of marketplace GCs in our 24/7 CFE performance in the future. Looking ahead, these tools will become even more important to develop. The recently released net zero standard of the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) will require reporting on hourly matching performance for large energy users, and the GHG Protocol (GHGP) is evaluating the introduction of hourly emissions reporting. We will continue to work on developing and advancing GCs — not just for our own efforts, but to ensure others can use these tools to build a better energy system. title: Build strategic A/B tests to grow your ad performance.
body: Google Ads Build strategic A/B tests to grow your ad performance. Nov 19, 2026 In an era of rapid AI innovation, experimentation can serve as a strategic compass. In the latest episode of Ads Decoded, Ads Product Liaison Ginny Marvin sits down with product leads Sagar Shah and Al Nevarez to explore how A/B testing validates AI Max features, budget shifts, and Smart Bidding strategies. Three key rules to guide your testing: Start with templated setups: Pre-built templates isolate single variables, split traffic 50/50, and minimize setup errors for cleaner data. Focus on business outcomes: Measure qualified conversions rather than shallow proxies, and give tests four to six weeks to account for conversion lag. Match confidence to decision scope: An 80% confidence interval works well for directional tweaks. Reserve 95% certainty for major structural overhauls. Explore the Experiments tab in Google Ads, test with confidence, and let data prove the value before scaling. Listen here.

title: Jefferson, Monetary Policy amid Frequent and Complex Shocks
body:
﻿ Speech by Vice Chair Jefferson on economic shocks - Federal Reserve Board Skip to main content An official website of the United States Government Here's how you know Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States.           the nation with a safe, flexible, and stable monetary and financial
          system. Main Menu Toggle Button Sections Search Toggle Button Search Search Submit Button Submit Home News & Events Speeches Speech PDF November 19, 2026 Monetary Policy amid Frequent and Complex Shocks Vice Chair Philip N. Jefferson At the International Monetary Fund and Central Bank of Brazil Conference “A Quarter Century of Inflation Targeting in Latin America:  Progress, Challenges, and the Road Ahead,” Brasília, Brazil Share Watch Live Thank you, Nigel, for that kind introduction, and thank you to the Central Bank of Brazil and International Monetary Fund for hosting this important conference. 1 It is an honor to be here with my fellow panelists. Today, I will briefly discuss issues that are critical for central bankers around the world—that is, how to assess and confront economic shocks. I discussed these issues in more depth in a speech earlier this year at Stanford University. 2 Shocks, by their nature, are difficult to predict and vary in length, but we are nonetheless very familiar with them. Just in the past few years, we have experienced a pandemic, a rapid rise in energy prices associated with geopolitical tensions, changes to trade policy, and a technological breakthrough. One way to classify shocks is to determine whether their initial effect is on the demand side or the supply side of the economy. Demand shocks affect spending by households, businesses, or the government without changing productive capacity. Supply shocks change productive capacity—what economists call "potential output"—by affecting the available supply of labor and capital or the productivity of those inputs. The nature and duration of these shocks influence the approach to monetary policymaking. As a monetary policymaker in the United States, I must consider whether and how shocks impact both sides of our dual mandate—maximum employment and stable prices. When a shock moves the output gap and inflation in the same direction, our objectives are aligned, and policy actions taken to address one also support the other. 3 When a shock pushes them in opposite directions, there is a tradeoff. The recent rise in oil prices tied to the conflict in the Middle East is an example of the latter. An energy price shock can push up inflation while weighing on real incomes and demand. The appropriate response depends on the relative costs of missing each objective and the balance of risks. When the recent energy price shock occurred, inflation in the U.S. was already above our 2 percent target. If inflation expectations risk becoming unanchored, a stronger reaction to inflation is warranted. If price pressures are contained, it may be prudent to prioritize downside risks to employment. Shocks that affect both aggregate supply and aggregated demand but with differential timing are especially challenging for monetary policymakers. The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) represents such a shock. Business adoption of AI has risen considerably over the past two years. 4 On the demand side, optimism about the technology has been boosting business investment in data centers, advanced computing equipment, and related products. On the supply side, AI is likely to automate some tasks and augment others, which could raise productivity and, in turn, the growth rate of potential output. Currently, the AI buildout is exerting upward pressure on demand and inflation. In the future, advancements in productivity could exert downward pressure on inflation while continuing to support growth. Labor market effects are relevant as well. AI could cause some job displacement, a meaningful challenge for affected households. Like many technological breakthroughs of the past, however, AI could lead to the creation of new jobs and new firms that we have not yet imagined. Shocks do not arrive in a vacuum. Energy, trade, and AI shocks are all unfolding at once. My colleagues at the Fed and my peers around the world must weigh them simultaneously. Our task is to remain attentive to our respective mandates and to keep the stance of our policies appropriately calibrated to achieve those stated goals. For the U.S. economy, my goal is to restore price stability while maintaining a solid labor market. That outcome will help the economy grow according to its full potential. Thank you, and I look forward to our discussion. 1. The views expressed here are my own and are not necessarily those of my colleagues on the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. Return to text 2. See Philip N. Jefferson, " Navigating Economic Shocks: A Monetary Policymaker's Perspective ," speech delivered at the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research, Stanford University, Stanford, CA, July 16, 2026. Return to text 3. The output gap is the difference between the economy's actual output, typically measured by GDP, and an estimate of its potential output. A positive gap signals excess demand, with employment above its maximum sustainable level and upward pressure on inflation; a negative gap signals excess supply, with the opposite effects. Return to text 4. Recent technological advancements discussed in this speech are sometimes referred to as super intelligence or SI. Return to text Last Update:
                
                            November 19, 2026 Back to Top

title: Season’s Streamings and Savings: Black Friday Deals Come to GeForce NOW
body: Season’s Streamings and Savings: Black Friday Deals Come to GeForce NOW Plus, bring PC gaming to more Fire TV Stick devices with a special sale, and stream five Bethesda favorites from GOG as part of nine games this week. November 19, 2026 by GeForce NOW Community 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! GeForce NOW is kicking off Black Friday with more reasons to make time for gaming. Six-month memberships are back for a limited time. Save 30% on the first six-month term of a Performance or Ultimate membership . Big gaming plans, smaller price tag. Keep the holiday savings going: Check out more NVIDIA holiday deals for gamers, creators and AI enthusiasts. The living room gets a little more playtime, too. GeForce NOW arrives on Amazon Fire TV Stick HD, Fire TV Stick 4K Select and Fire TV Stick 4K (2026 model) running Vega OS, alongside an Amazon offer launching later today for 90% off the first month of an eligible Performance or Ultimate membership in participating countries. It brings console-style gaming to the TV, straight from the Amazon cart. Bethesda fans have more in store, with five favorites adding GOG support as part of nine games joining GeForce NOW this week. Big RTX Power, Black Friday Price Thousands of games are calling from the cloud. Six-month Performance and Ultimate memberships are back for Black Friday, with 30% off the first six months for new memberships and eligible upgrades in select regions. The sale runs through Monday, Nov. 30, while supplies last. Go Ultimate for GeForce RTX 5080-class performance across PCs, Macs, Steam Deck and other supported handhelds, browsers, mobile devices, compatible TVs and more . Sessions lasting up to eight hours and first-priority server access leave more room for marathon play. Ultimate brings the latest NVIDIA innovations to the cloud, including DLSS 5 technology with the 3D-Guided Neural Rendering feature for lifelike lighting and materials in NBA 2K27 and Hogwarts Legacy , with support coming to War Thunder and Where Winds Meet . The experience goes big with streaming at up to 5K resolution or up to 360 frames per second, plus high dynamic range, ultrawide support and saved in-game settings. DLSS Super Resolution, Multi Frame Generation and Ray Reconstruction enhance supported games, including the path-traced missions of 007 First Light and the reality-bending action of CONTROL Resonant , while NVIDIA Reflex and Cloud G-SYNC technologies help keep gameplay responsive and smooth. GeForce NOW handles downloads, patches and updates for Ready-to-Play games, freeing local storage and leaving more time for gaming. Choose a membership and start the season streaming. More Screens, Major Savings Press play on more possibilities. GeForce NOW officially expands to all three of Amazon’s Vega OS streaming media players including Fire TV Stick HD, Fire TV Stick 4K Select and Fire TV Stick 4K (2026 model) bringing thousands of supported games to more another screens in the home. Vega OS keeps Fire TV fast and responsive, so launching GeForce NOW and jumping into games feels quick and snappy, with no console required. Getting started is simple: download the GeForce NOW app on a supported Fire TV device , sign in and connect a compatible controller. From cozy stories to epic adventures, turn-based tactics to co-op challenges, there’s plenty to build, explore and share with friends — all from the comfort of the couch. There’s a fire deal to get the games going, too. Launching later today through Thursday, Dec. 31, get 90% off the first month of a Performance or Ultimate membership purchased directly through Amazon on supported Fire TV devices in participating regions. The cloud is ready. The next quest is calling. GOG Big or Go Home Five favorite worlds. Extra ways to play. Five Bethesda titles expand their GeForce NOW support this week with their GOG versions: Indiana Jones and the Great Circle , Fallout 4 , The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim , DOOM and DOOM Eternal . Uncover an ancient mystery in Indiana Jones and the Great Circle , a first-person adventure set between Raiders of the Lost Ark and The Last Crusade . Explore the wasteland in Fallout 4 or trade the Pip-Boy for dragons and open-world fantasy in The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim . For a faster change of pace, DOOM brings relentless enemies, destructive weapons and fast-moving first-person combat, while its sequel, DOOM Eternal , turns up the intensity as the Slayer takes on demonic forces. Members who own the newly supported GOG versions can stream those titles through GeForce NOW without purchasing them again. From treasure hunts to dragon hunts, the collection can follow across nearly any supported device. Familiar worlds, with a little more room to roam. Members can look for the following games joining the GeForce NOW library this week: Volvy’s Adventure: Reslimed (New release on Steam , Nov. 19) Baldur’s Gate 3 ( Xbox Play Anywhere) DOOM (2016) ( GOG ) DOOM Eternal ( GOG ) Fallout 4 ( GOG ) Graveyard Keeper 2 ( Epic Games Store and GOG ) Indiana Jones and the Great Circle ( GOG ) Moon Sweepers ( Steam ) The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Anniversary Edition ( GOG ) Dates listed above reflect when games are released on their respective stores. GeForce NOW availability may vary, as games are onboarded after release and added throughout the week. Keep an eye on GeForce NOW channels and GFN Thursdays for availability updates on announced titles. Make it a cloud gaming weekend. Grab a day pass to try Performance or Ultimate before committing to a monthly membership, with the day pass cost applicable toward that first month. What’s on the big-screen gaming lineup this weekend? Let us know on X or in the comments below. body: We’re partnering with Blue Origin on our first heavy-lift Project Suncatcher launch. Travis Beals Senior Director, Paradigms of Intelligence Nov 19, 2026 We’re partnering with Blue Origin on the first heavy-lift launch for Project Suncatcher, our long-term moonshot to scale AI infrastructure in space by tapping into the abundant solar power in orbit. Targeted for Q1 2029, Blue Origin’s heavy-lift New Glenn rocket will deploy our satellites — each with roughly the capacity of a data center rack — into sun-synchronous orbit. This dedicated launch builds on our ongoing work with other satellite and launch partners and represents a crucial milestone on our long-term roadmap as we expand the boundaries of what's possible for the future of compute.

title: Pulaski County Man Sentenced for Armed Methamphetamine Trafficking
Stockton man indicted for possessing 16,000 carfentanil-laced pills, 57 pounds of methamphetamine, and 13 firearms
body: Press Release Stockton man indicted for possessing 16,000 carfentanil-laced pills, 57 pounds of methamphetamine, and 13 firearms Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of California SACRAMENTO, Calif. — A federal grand jury returned a three-count indictment today against Peter Anthony Zile, 60, of Stockton, charging him with possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine and carfentanil and with being a felon in possession of a firearm, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced. According to court documents, officers on the Delta Regional Auto Theft Team (RATT) found a stolen Ford F-350 parked in the driveway of Zile’s residence. During the execution of a search warrant at the residence, officers seized approximately 57 pounds of crystal methamphetamine, 13 firearms, several high-capacity magazines, approximately 4,390 rounds of ammunition, and more than $250,000 in cash. Agents also seized approximately 16,000 counterfeit M30 pills containing carfentanil, a dangerous synthetic opioid related to fentanyl. Zile is in custody pending trial. He is prohibited from possessing firearms or ammunition because of prior felony convictions including stalking, possession of a controlled substance for sale, and elder abuse. Homeland Security Investigations, the California Highway Patrol, the Stockton Police Department, and the San Joaquin County Sheriff’s Office conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Charles Campbell is prosecuting the case. If convicted, Zile faces a maximum statutory penalty of life years in prison, a mandatory minimum of 10 years in prison, and a $10 million fine. Any sentence, however, would be determined at the discretion of the court after consideration of any applicable statutory factors and the federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account a number of variables. The charges are only allegations; the defendant is presumed innocent until and unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. Updated November 19, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Component USAO - California, Eastern

title: 15 Members And Associates Of Gorilla Stone Bloods Gang Charged With Narcotics And Firearms Offenses In Sara D. Roosevelt Park
body: Press Release 15 Members And Associates Of Gorilla Stone Bloods Gang Charged With Narcotics And Firearms Offenses In Sara D. Roosevelt Park Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of New York United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the New York Field Office of Homeland Security Investigations (“HSI”), Pete Gizas, Special Agent in Charge of the New York Task Force Division of the Drug Enforcement Administration (“DEA”), Christopher Roberts, and Commissioner of the New York City Police Department (“NYPD”), Jessica S. Tisch, announced today the unsealing of an Indictment charging 15 members and associates of the Untouchable Gorilla Stone Nation (“Gorilla Stone”), a set of the nationwide Bloods street gang, with conspiring to distribute crack cocaine, heroin, fentanyl, and synthetic cannabinoids in and around Sara D. Roosevelt Park (“SDR Park”) in the Lower East Side of Manhattan.  Some defendants were additionally charged with possessing firearms, some of which were brandished and discharged, in furtherance of their narcotics trafficking.  Six of the defendants were in New York City or New York State custody and brought into federal custody, with eight of the remaining nine defendants arrested and presented in federal court.  The case is assigned to U.S. District Judge Lewis J. Liman. “Our Office will stop at nothing to keep New Yorkers and our community safe,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald.  “This is particularly true for public spaces in New York, like our parks. As alleged, for years a violent gang network operated an open-air drug market that poisoned the Lower East Side of Manhattan with fentanyl, heroin, crack cocaine, and K2.  The defendants allegedly trafficked deadly drugs while arming themselves with illegal firearms and engaging in brutal violence to protect their turf.  Gang-driven narcotics trafficking inflicts enormous harm on neighborhoods and families. New Yorkers should know that they can count on our Office and our law enforcement partners to protect them from these harms.” “Today’s arrests strike a major blow against this gang who is accused of using fear, violence, narcotics sales, and illegal guns to control the streets and parks of a New York City community,” said HSI Acting Special Agent in Charge Pete Gizas.  “New Yorkers deserve safe neighborhoods, not ones ruled by violent criminal organizations.  We will combat these violent gangs with decisive law enforcement might.  HSI New York, alongside the U.S. Attorney’s Office, NYPD, DEA, and all our law enforcement partners, will relentlessly pursue those responsible and hold them accountable.” “All New Yorkers deserve the right to live, work, and enjoy public spaces and parks free from drugs, gangs, and violence,” said DEA New York Task Force Division Special Agent in Charge Christopher Roberts.  “These defendants allegedly turned the Sara D. Roosevelt Park into an open-air drug market, using fear, intimidation, and brutal violence to control areas of the park and terrorize this community.  From vicious slashings and stabbings to shootings and armed assaults, these violent acts demonstrated the dangerous lengths these individuals used to protect their criminal enterprise and exert control over our neighborhoods.  Today, those days are over!  The DEA and our law enforcement partners will not stand idle while violent gangs attempt to take over our parks and neighborhoods.  Our public spaces belong to the people, not drug traffickers and criminals.” “As alleged, these defendants, part of the Untouchable Gorilla Stone Nation gang, turned a Lower East Side park into their own open-air drug market and violent playground,” said NYPD Commissioner Jessica S. Tisch.  “This takedown is yet another example of the diligent work our investigators do to dismantle dangerous gangs and stop the illegal drug businesses that threaten our communities.  I thank our dedicated NYPD detectives, law enforcement partners, and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York for their shared commitment to making New York City safer.” According to the Indictment and public court filings:(1) Between approximately 2023 and 2026, the defendants were members or associates of the Gorilla Stone gang and took over SDR Park, in the heart of the Lower East Side, with violence and fear through the trafficking of crack cocaine, heroin, fentanyl, and synthetic cannabinoids or K2.  The defendants had established agreements, understandings, and practices that governed how they operated and how their different members coexisted within the same drug-dealing territory.  For example, the defendants divided SDR Park, with certain dealers controlling different parts of the Park.  While these dealers permitted one another to sell in close physical proximity, they did not allow outsiders or newcomers to sell in their territory and worked together, often using violence to keep out rival or unfamiliar drug dealers.  The defendants also exercised control over the Park by working in shifts.  By agreement and with proactive coordination, certain dealers, along with their workers, sold in the morning, while others sold in the evening or overnight.  In addition, the defendants warned each other about law enforcement’s presence in the area, shared suppliers (and several defendants and other members of the conspiracy themselves supplied narcotics to other defendants), steered customers to each other, provided each other with narcotics when someone ran out, and jointly responded to threats that might impact any dealer in SDR Park. To protect and further its drug business, certain of the defendants engaged in frequent acts of violence, including committing slashings, stabbings, robberies, and gun violence against rival drug dealers in the area and their own narcotics customers, typically drug-addicted individuals.  For instance: In December 2024, in the vicinity of SDR Park, Ibrahim Toure, a/k/a “Fah,” sold K2 to a customer who paid Toure with counterfeit cash.  Toure slashed the victim twice, once to the top of his head and once to his face, as depicted below. In February 2026, in the vicinity of SDR Park, Matthew Newman, a/k/a “Money,” participated in the stabbing of a victim whose close friend had a narcotics-related debt to Newman.  Specifically, Newman gave a blade to an uncharged coconspirator, who stabbed the victim seven times in the back, resulting in a collapsed lung and bleeding from a kidney. In April 2026, in the vicinity of SDR Park, Newman, Basil Simms, a/k/a “Sheff,” Sean Sims, a/k/a “Vito,” and one unidentified perpetrator assaulted and stabbed another drug dealer who was selling K2 at under-market prices.  A photo of the victim’s leg is depicted below. In July 2026, CAMERON BARNHILL, a/k/a “Baby Ape,” and ASHANTE INNISS, a/k/a “Fire,” with other perpetrators, assaulted and robbed a competitor drug dealer near SDR Park, including by stomping on his face and neck and by beating him with a traffic cone.  A screenshot of the assault is depicted below: In May 2024, NEWMAN, with two other perpetrators, committed a gang-related assault, including a pistol-whipping, of another Gorilla Stone member who was perceived to be a disfavored member of the gang.  Screenshots of NEWMAN committing the gang assault, which took place near SDR Park, are depicted below: Several members of Gorilla Stone, including some of the defendants, also possessed and carried firearms in and around SDR Park, including to have firearms available in the event of a dispute.  For example, from approximately 2024 to 2025, Sims, then a member of another Bloods set, engaged in a series of back-and-forth acts of violence with Newman regarding, among other things, their respective drug-dealing territory and influence in SDR Park.  Following a March 2025 incident in which Newman and Sims slashed each other, Sims determined that he wanted to join Gorilla Stone to avoid continued fighting with Newman.  Newman provided Sims with a gun and told him to shoot an enemy of Gorilla Stone.  On or about April 19, 2026, Sims and an uncharged coconspirator shot a 16-year-old victim in the upper thigh, as depicted below.  The victim was hospitalized. *                *                * A chart containing the defendants’ names, charges, and maximum penalties is set forth below. The maximum potential sentences in this case are prescribed by Congress and provided here for informational purposes only, as any sentencing of the defendants will be determined by the judge. Mr. McDonald thanked HSI, DEA, and the NYPD for their exceptional investigative work, as well as the Digital Forensics Unit, and the Complex Analytics and Social Media Enhancement Team at the New York/New Jersey High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York.  Mr. McDonald further thanked the United States Marshals Service for their assistance and partnership. This case is being handled by the Office’s Narcotics Unit.  Assistant U.S. Attorneys Remy Grosbard, Kevin Grossinger, Mostafa Khairy, and Lauren E. Phillips are in charge of the prosecution. The charges contained in the Indictment are merely accusations, and the defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. title: A Total of Fourteen Illegal Aliens Sentenced to Prison in Three Separate Conspiracies and for Possessing Property Stolen from Multiple Burglaries
body: Press Release A Total of Fourteen Illegal Aliens Sentenced to Prison in Three Separate Conspiracies and for Possessing Property Stolen from Multiple Burglaries Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Jersey NEWARK, N.J. – Since 2025, fourteen Chilean nationals, present in the United States illegally and believed to be part of three South American theft groups, pleaded guilty and were sentenced to imprisonment for engaging in multiple conspiracies involving burglaries in New Jersey and elsewhere, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced. Flavio Bladimir Astete Castillo, Dareyen Mauricio Cortes-Canete, Luis Esteban Castillo Vivar, Max Vidal Navarrete, Jordán Estefano Contreras Vilches, and Juan Jose Ramirez Nilo, all of Chile, were each charged by criminal complaint in May 2024 and each pleaded guilty to conspiracy and to possessing stolen property taken from residential burglaries, including in New Jersey, which was transported over state lines. Christofer Sanguesa Aguirre, Fabiana Prado Scatarzi, Santana Arturo Castillo Gonzalez, Felipe Andres Del Valle Munoz, Carlos Alfredo Calderon Valencia, Diego Antonio Calderon Leiva, and Pedro Alejandro Salgado Vallejos, all of Chile, were each charged by criminal complaint in January 2025 and each pleaded guilty to conspiracy and possessing stolen property taken from residential burglaries, including in New Jersey, which was transported over state lines. Gustavo Ignacio Salas Ortega, also of Chile, was charged by criminal complaint in February 2025 and pleaded guilty to conspiracy and possessing stolen property taken from a burglary of a jewelry store in New Jersey, which was transported over state lines. All of the defendants were sentenced to terms of imprisonment of between 15 and 30 months, as shown in the table below. Defendant Date of Sentence U.S. District Judge Prison Sentence Vidal Navarrete Oct. 22, 2025 Claire C. Cecchi Time served (approx. 17 months) Castillo Vivar Nov. 4, 2025 Claire C. Cecchi 27 months Contreras Vilches Nov. 13, 2025 Claire C. Cecchi 27 months Ramirez Nilo Nov. 20, 2025 Claire C. Cecchi Time served (approx. 18 months) Cortes-Canete Feb. 26, 2026 Claire C. Cecchi Time served (approx. 21 months) Astete Castillo Mar. 18, 2026 Claire C. Cecchi Time served (approx. 22 months) Del Valle Munoz Apr. 9, 2026 Christine P. O’Hearn Time served (approx. 15 months) Prado Scatarzi Apr. 13, 2026 Christine P. O’Hearn Time served (approx. 15 months) Sanguesa Aguirre June 2, 2026 Christine P. O’Hearn Time served (approx. 16 months) Salgado Vallejos June 8, 2026 Christine P. O’Hearn Time served (approx. 17 months) Castillo Gonzalez June 18, 2026 Christine P. O’Hearn 22 months Salas Ortega Oct. 26, 2026 Michael A. Shipp 30 months Calderon Leiva Nov. 17, 2026 Christine P. O’Hearn 21 months Calderon Valencia Nov. 17, 2026 Christine P. O’Hearn 27 months “These fourteen defendants engaged in sophisticated, highly organized burglaries that targeted residences and businesses in New Jersey and beyond.  They did significant damage to the victims’ lives, invaded their private spaces, and put the public in danger. My office and our law enforcement partners are committed to finding perpetrators like these and preventing them from harming innocent people in New Jersey and across the United States.” - U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer “By design, these criminal tourists left behind very few clues when committing these burglaries. They used their nomadic lifestyle to cloak their identities and movements, believing it would help them evade detection,” said FBI Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy.  “What they could not have foreseen was the determination of the agents and task force officers assigned to the Newark FBI Joint Organized Crime Task Force, who meticulously gathered evidence and collaborated with partners across the country. To other thieves who operate in the same way: justice will find you.” “Fourteen Chilean nationals who were unlawfully present in the United States preyed on law-abiding Americans by participating in organized burglary and theft schemes that targeted residences, businesses, and valuable property across New Jersey and beyond,” said ICE-ERO Acting Field Office Director Tammy Marich. “After entering and remaining in this country in violation of our immigration laws, they demonstrated a calculated disregard for the people they victimized, the safety of our communities, and the rule of law. ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations Newark remains committed to identifying, arresting, and removing criminal illegal aliens who exploit law-abiding members of our communities.” According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court: Astete Castillo, Cortes-Canete, Castillo Vivar, Vidal Navarrete, Contreras Vilches, and Ramirez Nilo were part of a burglary ring that committed multiple residential burglaries in March and April 2024 in multiple states, including New Jersey, Maryland, and New York. The defendants stole large amounts of jewelry, collectibles, and other valuables from the residences. Sanguesa Aguirre, Prado Scatarzi, Castillo Gonzalez, Del Valle Munoz, Calderon Valencia, Calderon Leiva, and Salgado Vallejos were part of a sophisticated burglary ring that committed multiple residential burglaries in November 2024 in New Jersey and Massachusetts.  The defendants broke into homes, stole jewelry, watches, designer handbags, and other valuable goods, and then traveled with them to other states. At the scene of one burglary, in Massachusetts, the defendants destroyed precious keepsakes that included the cremated remains of a loved one, which the residents had stored in their home. The defendants also used signal jamming devices to interfere with security alarm systems while committing the burglaries. When several of the defendants were arrested by immigration authorities in November 2024, Del Valle Munoz and Calderon Valencia fled across the country, eventually appearing near Seattle, Washington before traveling to a residence in Carlton, Oregon. Law enforcement searched the residence where Del Valle Munoz, Calderon Valencia, and others had arrived and recovered bags and backpacks containing additional gold jewelry, diamonds, and watches, along with burglary tools and jamming devices. Castillo Gonzalez also pleaded guilty and was sentenced for possessing a contraband cell phone after he was arrested and pending trial in a detention facility used to house federal detainees. Salas Ortega was part of a third group that scouted a jewelry store in a New Jersey mall before committing a burglary of the jewelry store by cutting a hole through an adjacent wall. The group also used a wireless security camera to watch for security guards while they committed the burglary. Law enforcement later found Salas Ortega wearing an expensive wristwatch that had been in the jewelry store at the time of the burglary. The defendant was seen on surveillance cameras wearing the stolen wristwatch in New York on multiple days after the burglary. In addition to the prison terms, Judge Cecci, Judge Shipp, and Judge O’Hearn each ordered the respective defendants to pay restitution to the victims of the conspiracies. The restitution judgments totaled $2,591,323.82. U.S. Attorney Frazer credited the FBI Newark’s Joint Organized Crime Task Force (JOCTF), under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy in Newark; Immigration and Customs Enforcement – Enforcement and Removal Operations, under the direction of Field Office Director Tammy Marich; the Millburn Police Department under the direction of Chief Brian Gilfedder; the Clinton Township Police Department, under the direction of Chief Thomas A. DeRosa, and the Denver Police Department, under the direction of Chief Ron Thomas, with the investigations leading to the sentences. He also thanked the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey Police Department, Warren Township Police Department, Amtrak Police Department, Baltimore County Police Burglary Unit, Jersey City Police Department, Los Angeles Police Department, New York State Police, Westchester County Police, NJ Transit Police, Colts Neck Police Department, Keansburg Police Department, Fort Lee Police Department, Paramus Police Department, New Jersey State Police, Spring Valley Police Department (NY), Town of Greenburgh Police Department (NY), Wellesley Police Department (MA), Westwood Police Department (MA), Massachusetts State Police, Renton Police Department (WA), King County Sheriff’s Office (WA), Tukwila Police Department (WA), Oregon State Police, Yamhill County Sheriff’s Office (OR), Carlton Police Department (OR), Pennsylvania State Police, Novi Police Department (MI), Denver District Attorney’s Office, Essex County Prosecutor’s Office, Monmouth County Prosecutor’s Office, ICE/ERO Portland, ICE/ERO Seattle, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, FBI Denver, FBI New York, FBI Philadelphia, FBI Seattle, FBI Portland, FBI New Orleans, FBI Boston, FBI Los Angeles, DEA Newark, Policía de Investigaciones de Chile (PDI), and the FBI Legal Attaché Santiago, Chile. Finally, U.S. Attorney Frazer thanked the Jewelers’ Security Alliance for its support of the investigations. The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Trevor A. Chenoweth of the Cybercrime Unit in Newark. ### Defense counsel: Flavio Bladimir Astete Castillo: Maximillian Novel Esq., Jersey City, New Jersey Dareyen Mauricio Cortes-Canete: Michael T. title: Puyallup, Washington, man sentenced to five years in prison for trafficking deadly form of fentanyl
body: Press Release Puyallup, Washington, man sentenced to five years in prison for trafficking deadly form of fentanyl Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Washington Defendant possessed more than 50,000 carfentanil pills – a drug used to sedate large animals such as elephants Tacoma – A 37-year-old Puyallup, Washington, resident was sentenced today in U.S. District Court in Tacoma to 60 months in prison for possession of controlled substances with intent to distribute, announced Acting U.S. Attorney Charles Neil Floyd. Nathaniel Washington was arrested near Centralia, Washington, on September 16, 2025. In Washington’s car were more than 50,000 pills of carfentanil – an opioid 100 times stronger than fentanyl. “Mr. Washington’s shipment was sure to bring death to drug users in western Washington. This drug is designed to sedate large animals such as elephants – putting it in a pill designed to look like oxycontin endangers addicts and casual users alike,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Floyd. “Stopping this load of drugs saved lives and has earned this defendant his federal prison time.” “Mr. Washington demonstrated a complete disregard for human life when he transported a load of deadly carfentanil pills to Western Washington for distribution,” said Robert A. Saccone, Special Agent in Charge, DEA Seattle Field Division. “Carfentanil is a synthetic opioid developed to tranquilize large animals and is estimated to be 100 times more potent than fentanyl. The potential devastation posed by more than 50,000 of these pills cannot be overstated. This seizure by DEA and our law enforcement partners prevented an enormous amount of harm. Let this sentence serve as a warning: DEA and our law enforcement partners will aggressively pursue those who traffic these deadly substances and hold them accountable.” According to records filed in the case, Washington came to the attention of law enforcement as the source of supply for a local drug trafficking ring. Law enforcement learned Washington regularly traveled to Arizona to pick up drugs, rented a car, and drove them into Western Washington for their eventual distribution on the illegal market. On September 15, law enforcement tracked Washington as he again followed this pattern – flying into Phoenix, Arizona, and beginning the drive back to Western Washington in a rental car only five hours later. This time, a DEA task force officer followed behind Washington as he pulled into a service station off I-5 heading northbound. Law enforcement detained Washington and a drug-detecting canine alerted to the car. Officers found two large vacuum-sealed bags containing 50,208 small blue pills imprinted with “M30” concealed in the lining of a suitcase in Washington’s trunk. Lab testing revealed the pills contained carfentanil, a powerful fentanyl analog used in veterinary medicine. It is 100 times stronger than fentanyl and 10,000 times stronger than morphine. DEA issued a warning when the pills were seized: when the pills were seized: Warning: Thousands of Counterfeit M30 Pills Containing Carfentanil Seized in Western Washington Nathaniel Washington was indicted by the grand jury on September 24, 2025, and pleaded guilty on July 27, 2026. In asking for a six-year sentence prosecutors wrote to the court, “The record reflects Washington has been engaging in illegal drug transactions without detection for some time. Certainly, a courier is not entrusted with the quantity of drugs Washington was caught carrying without established relationships and a proven history in the trade.” U.S. District Judge Tiffany M. Cartwright ordered Washington to be on four years of supervised release following prison. The case was jointly investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF). The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Victoria Cantore. Contact Press contact for the U.S. Attorney’s Office is Communications Director Emily Langlie at (206) 553-4110 or Emily.Langlie@usdoj.gov . title: Dulce Man Sentenced for Violent Assault
body: Press Release Dulce Man Sentenced for Violent Assault Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Mexico ALBUQUERQUE – A Dulce man was sentenced to 27 months in prison for a violent assault that left the victim with serious injuries. According to court documents, on December 31, 2025, Dennison Billy, Jr. , 36, an enrolled member of the Navajo Nation, struck an adult victim in the face with his fists while the victim was driving a vehicle in Dulce, New Mexico. Responding officers found Billy highly intoxicated in the passenger seat and the victim nearby with visible blood and multiple injuries. The victim reported exiting the vehicle to avoid further assault and was transported to a local hospital for treatment. Billy told law enforcement that he had consumed a large amount of alcohol, blacked out, and did not remember the incident. The victim sustained serious injuries, including fractures to the orbital wall and nasal bones. Billy pleaded guilty to assault resulting in serious bodily injury. There is no parole in the federal system. Upon his release from prison, Billy will be subject to three years of supervised release. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison and Special Agent in Charge Justin A. Garris of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office made the announcement today. The Farmington Resident Agency of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office investigated this case with assistance from the Jicarilla Apache Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Aaron O. Jordan is prosecuting the case. title: Laramie man sentenced to 30 years in federal prison for sexual exploitation of a minor and possession of child sexual abuse material
body: Press Release Laramie man sentenced to 30 years in federal prison for sexual exploitation of a minor and possession of child sexual abuse material Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Wyoming usawy.pio@usdoj.gov CHEYENNE, Wyo. — Michael Collins Guenzel , 24, of Laramie, has been sentenced to 30 years in federal prison, followed by 10 years of supervised release, for sexual exploitation of a minor and child sexual abuse material offenses. U.S. District Court Judge Alan B. Johnson imposed the sentence. According to court documents, Guenzel was 23 years old and serving a term of felony probation in Albany County, Wyoming, when he posed online as a 16-year-old boy to target and groom a 13-year-old victim. Continuing to misrepresent his age and identity, Guenzel met the child at a hotel and sexually abused her. The crimes came to light after Guenzel’s state probation officer searched his phone and discovered sexually explicit files depicting a young girl. Upon learning of the subsequent law enforcement investigation, Guenzel texted associates and instructed them not to speak with police. On July 10, 2026, Guenzel pleaded guilty to eight federal felony counts: five counts of sexual exploitation of a minor, one count of travel with intent to engage in illicit sexual conduct with a minor, one count of receipt of child sexual abuse material and one count of possession of child sexual abuse material. “Justice cannot erase the lasting harm done to this poor girl, but today’s sentence ensures this predator is held accountable,” said U.S. Attorney Darin Smith. “This result is a testament to the unwavering dedication of the Laramie Police Department and the Wyoming Division of Criminal Investigation's Internet Crimes Against Children team.” “After the probation officer discovered concerning files on the phone, they contacted LPD and we were able to kick off this investigation, ultimately turning it over to DCI’s ICAC team for completion and leading it to a successful prosecution through the U.S. Attorney’s Office,” said Taun Smith, deputy chief of the Laramie Police Department. “This outcome is a direct result of teamwork across our criminal justice system, from the vigilance of state probation and the partnership of the Laramie Police Department to the dedicated investigators of our Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force and the prosecutor at the U.S. Attorney’s Office,” said Ryan Cox, commander of the Wyoming Division of Criminal Investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Mackenzie R. Morrison prosecuted the crime. This case was part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide Department of Justice initiative launched to combat child sexual exploitation and abuse. Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. More information is available at justice.gov/psc . ### Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Components Criminal - Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section Defending Childhood Department of Justice USAO - Wyoming Press Release Number: 26-056

title: Previously Convicted Sex Offender Sentenced for Ninth Supervised Release Violation
body: Press Release Previously Convicted Sex Offender Sentenced for Ninth Supervised Release Violation Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Mexico ALBUQUERQUE – A previously convicted sex offender was sentenced to 81 months in prison for failing to update his sex offender registration and for violating the terms of his supervised release by failing to reside at a location approved by his probation officer. According to court documents, on December 29, 2025, Chebon Joe Wilson , 43, was released from prison after serving a 10-month sentence for his eighth violation of supervised release related to a 2010 conviction for abusive sexual contact. He was ordered to report to a sober living program that same day but failed to do so and did not promptly notify his probation officer of his residence. Wilson was subsequently arrested in Albuquerque on April 15, 2026, and detained. On July 29, 2026, Wilson pleaded guilty to failing to update his sex offender registration. He was sentenced to 21 months in prison for failing to register and 60 months for violating the terms of his supervised release. The sentences will run consecutively, resulting in a total prison term of 81 months. Upon his release from prison, Wilson will be subject to five years of supervised release. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison and U.S. Marshal David Barnett for the District of New Mexico made the announcement today. The U.S. Marshals Service investigated this case. Assistant United States Attorney Seth Teleky prosecuted the case. Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Indian Country Law and Justice Components USAO - New Mexico U.S. Marshals Service Press Release Number: 26-323

title: Six Defendants Facing Federal Charges for their Roles in Alleged Human Trafficking Where Commercial Sex Acts Were Offered at Massage Parlors in Utah
body: Press Release Six Defendants Facing Federal Charges for their Roles in Alleged Human Trafficking Where Commercial Sex Acts Were Offered at Massage Parlors in Utah Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Utah As part of a Homeland Security Task Force led investigation, multiple defendants allegedly benefited financially from owning and operating massage parlors where a victim was coerced to engage in sexual activity SALT LAKE CITY – A federal grand jury returned an indictment charging six people – including three Chinese nationals, two of whom are illegally living in the United States – for their roles in the operation of illicit massage parlors from Orem to Ogden. As part of an undercover operation led by the Homeland Security Task Force, the alleged conduct revealed a victim was coerced into engaging in prostitution and living at a massage parlor. Yongzhen Yang, 60, a Chinese national living in Springville, Utah; Kristian Walker Bryant, 53, of Farr West, Utah; Jia Ming Zhou, 69, Chinese national living in Springville, Utah; Thomas Weyerts, 49, of Logan, Utah; and Marcus Pok Wan Chan, 38, of West Valley City, Utah, were charged by complaint on November 5. Kai Man Coco Lee, 49, of China, but previously lived in Farr West, Utah, was also indicted, along with the above defendants on November 18. According to court documents, on or about September 10, 2022, continuing through Oct. 31, in the District of Utah and elsewhere, Yang, Bryant, and Zhou enticed victim 1 to engage in a commercial sex acts, so the defendants could benefit financially. The investigation by Homeland Security Investigations revealed that Yang allegedly created and maintained several illicit massage businesses in Utah. These establishments, while operating under the guise of providing therapeutic massage services, functioned primarily as fronts for prostitution, commercial sexual exploitation, and human trafficking. As alleged, Yang would initially open various massage parlors and then sell them to others, including Bryant, and Zhou. Yang would then visit each parlor and collect proceeds from the illegal sex services provided at the parlors. As alleged in court documents, from August 15, 2019, through October 15, hundreds of advertisements were posted on websites listing various massage parlors registered by Yang, Bryant, or Zhou. These websites are known to host advertisements for sexual services and or escorts. The businesses are set for cash-only and victims have stated they only get paid if they perform sexual services. As further alleged in court documents, beginning on or about May 28, continuing through Nov. 4, Weyerts and Chan’s role in the illicit massage business was to allegedly launder money for the co-defendants. Weyerts and Chan allegedly coordinated money pickups and money deposits in various bank accounts and attempted to conceal the money by structuring deposits under $10,000.00. According to court documents, Yang is a Chinese national who overstayed on his visa in the United States and is subject of deportation proceedings. Yang has not been authorized to work in the United States since 2017. As alleged in court documents, Zhou is a Chinese national in the United States on a permanent residence card subject to expiration in 2032. She is the subject of an immigration hold resulting from this investigation. Lee, a Chinese national, and the spouse of defendant Bryant, is presently unable to return to the United States because of her lack of immigration status. All six defendants are charged with human trafficking conspiracy; sex trafficking by force, fraud, or coercion; and money laundering conspiracy. Bryant and Zhou are also charged with transporting individual to engage in prostitution. The defendants are scheduled for their initial appearances on the indictment before a U.S. Magistrate Judge at the Orrin G. Hatch United States Courthouse in downtown Salt Lake City. See docket for dates and times. United States Attorney Melissa Holyoak of the District of Utah made the announcement. The case is being investigated jointly by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI), Murray City Police Department, and the Orem Police Department. Valuable assistance was provided by the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Assistant United States Attorney Carlos A. Esqueda of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Utah is prosecuting the case. This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Salt Lake comprises agents and officers from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), and the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Utah. An indictment is merely an allegation and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law . Contact Felicia Martinez Public Affairs Specialist Felicia.martinez@usdoj.gov Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Homeland Security Task Force Component USAO - Utah Press Release Number: 26-122

title: California Man Sentenced to More Than 12 Years in Federal Prison for Trafficking Large Quantity of Cocaine
body: Press Release California Man Sentenced to More Than 12 Years in Federal Prison for Trafficking Large Quantity of Cocaine Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Arkansas Ms. Paulette Chappelle, Public Affairs Officer Paulette.Chappelle@usdoj.gov LITTLE ROCK—A trip from California to Memphis to deliver large amounts of narcotics ended prematurely in Arkansas for Claude Bell, who will now spend 151 months in federal prison for possession with intent to distribute five kilograms or more of cocaine. Jonathan D. Ross, United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Arkansas, announced the sentence, which was handed down today by Chief United States District Judge Kristine G. Baker. A federal grand jury indicted Bell, 58, of Lancaster, California, in a two-count Indictment for possession with intent to distribute cocaine and possession with intent to distribute fentanyl. On May 14, 2026, Bell pleaded guilty to possession with intent to distribute five kilograms or more of cocaine. Chief Judge Baker also sentenced Bell to five years’ supervised release. There is no parole in the federal system. On May 19, 2025, a trooper with the Arkansas State Police conducted a traffic stop in Russellville on a tractor-trailer being driven by Bell. During the traffic stop, the trooper observed Bell behaving nervously. Bell did not have a logbook to show his driving time and at that point, the trooper obtained consent from Bell to search the tractor and trailer. During a search of the sleeper area of the truck’s cab, the trooper located four boxes containing packages of approximately 86 pounds of cocaine and approximately 34 pounds of fentanyl. At that time, Bell was placed under arrest and agents from the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) arrived on scene and took custody of the packaged cocaine and fentanyl. During a post- Miranda interview, Bell admitted he was paid $30,000 to transport the cocaine from Bueno Park, California, to Memphis, Tennessee. Based on a search warrant, officers reviewed Bell’s cell phone which showed he picked up the boxes in California and was traveling to deliver them to an individual at a gas station in Memphis. Bell’s prior felony convictions, which date back to 1987, include robbery, vehicle grand theft, second degree burglary of a vehicle, second-degree robbery, and second-degree attempted burglary. This case was investigated by the DEA, with assistance from the Arkansas State Police, Fifth Judicial Drug Task Force, and the Central Arkansas Drug Task Force. This case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Shelby Shelton. Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Component USAO - Arkansas, Eastern
