title: Two Plead Guilty in D.C. to Trafficking Firearms from Virginia
body: Press Release Two Plead Guilty in D.C. to Trafficking Firearms from Virginia Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia WASHINGTON – Moniqua Jefferson, 31 and Valentino Hall, 28, both of Richmond, Virginia, pleaded guilty today in U.S. District Court to their roles in a conspiracy that trafficked firearms from Virginia into the Washington metropolitan region, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. Jefferson and Hall each pleaded guilty today before Judge Ana C. Reyes to a one count of conspiracy to commit trafficking in firearms. Judge Reyes scheduled Jefferson’s sentencing for March 19, 2027, and Hall’s sentencing for April 2, 2027. A third co-defendant, Derrick Boyd, Jr., 32, of Capitol Heights, Maryland, is scheduled for trial on July 14, 2027. According to court documents, from September 2022 through September 2024, Jefferson and Hall would determine what firearms were available from federally licensed firearm retailers in the Richmond area. They then solicited interest from individuals prohibited from possessing any firearms. After determining potential buyers, Jefferson and Hall bought the guns at the licensed firearms dealers and then resold them at a markup. Jefferson and Hall purchased 24 firearms between August 2022 and May 2025. Four of those guns were recovered by law enforcement in the District of Columbia from individuals who were forbidden by law to carry or possess those firearms. Another gun, a Palmetto State Armory PA-15, allegedly was recovered in Maryland at Boyd’s residence. Boyd is a previously convicted felon and prohibited from possessing any firearm. The investigation was conducted by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives Washington Field Division. The case is being prosecuted Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Brendan M. Horan, who is detailed to the U.S. Attorney’s Office from the United States Capitol Police, and Assistant U.S. Attorney Travis Wolf. 25cr195 Follow us on X , Instagram , and YouTube or at https://www.justice.gov/usao-dc Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - District of Columbia

Brazilian National Who Allegedly Led Fake Pill Operation Charged and Extradited From Panama Following Homeland Security Task Force Investigation
body: Press Release Brazilian National Who Allegedly Led Fake Pill Operation Charged and Extradited From Panama Following Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts Three co-conspirators also charged; two pill press machines, over 16 kilograms of counterfeit pills, over nine kilograms of crystal methamphetamine and five firearms seized BOSTON – A Brazilian national has been extradited from the Republic of Panama after being indicted by a federal grand jury in Boston for his alleged role in manufacturing and distributing tens of thousands of counterfeit pills containing methamphetamine. Bruno Teixeira Badaia, a/k/a “Bruno Badaya,” a/k/a “Bruno BA,” a/k/a “Bunno Sanny Silva,” 32, of Brazil, was indicted by a federal grand jury in June 2026 on one count of conspiracy to distribute and to possess with intent to distribute controlled substances (involving 50 grams or more of methamphetamine and 500 grams or more of a mixture and substance containing methamphetamine). Badaia was arrested in the Republic of Panama in September 2026 and was extradited to Massachusetts. He remains detained in federal custody following an initial appearance in federal court in Boston earlier today. Three others – Franklin Argueta, a/k/a “Frizz,” 30, of Lowell, Mass.; Luis Arias, a/k/a “Nacho,” 31, of Somerville, Mass.; and Alexis Hernandez, 27, of California – were also charged in the indictment. All four defendants were charged with conspiracy to distribute and to possess with intent to distribute controlled substances. Argueta was also charged with two counts of distribution of and possession with intent to distribute a controlled substance; one count of possession with intent to distribute controlled substances; and one count of carrying a firearm during and in relation to, and possessing a firearm in furtherance of, a drug-trafficking crime. Arias was also charged with one count of distribution of and possession with intent to distribute a controlled substance; one count of possession with intent to distribute controlled substances; and one count of possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug-trafficking crime. According to court documents, beginning in approximately March 2025, Badaia conspired with other the defendants to manufacture and distribute methamphetamine and pills containing methamphetamine. Between August 2025 and October 2025, law enforcement conducted controlled purchases of of pills from Argueta and Arias at locations in Middlesex and Suffolk counties in Massachusetts. On Jan. 14, 2026, Argueta is alleged to have taken approximately 10,000 such pills out of his residence in Lowell and sold them to an undercover officer at a location in Middlesex County. During a search of Argueta’s residence in February 2026, it is alleged that tens of thousands of counterfeit pills suspected to contain methamphetamine, at least 9 kilograms of crystal methamphetamine and two firearms were recovered. It is further alleged that a search of Arias’s residence resulted in the recovery of tens of thousands of additional counterfeit pills suspected to contain methamphetamine and an additional firearm. Separately, two pill press machines used to manufacture counterfeit pills and dozens of bags of filler material used in the manufacturing process were also recovered. The charge of conspiracy to distribute and to possess with intent to distribute controlled substances (involving 50 grams or more of methamphetamine or 500 grams or more of a mixture and substance containing methamphetamine) provides for a sentence of no less than 10 years in prison, at least five years and up to a lifetime of supervised release and a fine of $10 million. The charges of carrying a firearm during and in relation to, and possessing a firearm in furtherance of, a drug-trafficking crime, and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug-trafficking crime each provide for a sentence of no less than five years and up to life in prison, to be served consecutively to the sentence for other crimes, five years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Jarod A. Forget, Special Agent in Charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration, New England Field Division; Jeff Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in New England; and Thomas Greco, Special Agent in Charge of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives, Boston Field Division made the announcement. Valuable assistance was provided by Massachusetts State Police; United States Marshals Service; and the Lowell and Somerville Police Departments. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs worked with the Government of Panama to secure the arrest and extradition of Badaia. Assistant U.S. Attorney Samuel R. Feldman of the Narcotics & Money Laundering Unit is prosecuting the case. This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Boston is comprised of agents and officers from HSI, FBI, DEA, ATF, USMS, IRS-CI, USPIS, DOL-OIG and DSS, as well as several state and local law enforcement agencies, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Massachusetts. The details contained in the charging documents are allegations. The defendants are presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in the court of law. Updated November 19, 2026 Topics Homeland Security Task Force Drug Trafficking Component USAO - Massachusetts

title: New London Felon Sentenced to More Than 7 Years in Federal Prison for Firearm Offense, Violating Supervised Release
body: Press Release New London Felon Sentenced to More Than 7 Years in Federal Prison for Firearm Offense, Violating Supervised Release Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Connecticut David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, announced that NESTOR PAGAN, also known as Nestor Angel Vargas, 43, of New London, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge Kari A. Dooley in Bridgeport to 90 months of imprisonment and three years of supervised release for unlawfully possessing a firearm, and for violating the conditions of his supervised release from a prior federal conviction. According to court documents and statements made in court, on April 29, 2026, U.S. Probation officers, assisted by members of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), the Connecticut State Police, and the New London Police Department, conducted a search of Pagan’s residence in New London and found a 9mm Smith & Wesson handgun, a .22 caliber Intratec, Tec-22 handgun, a high capacity magazine and additional gun magazines, and numerous rounds of ammunition. At the time of the search, Pagan was on federal supervised release after being convicted of unlawful possession of a firearm by a felon in 2017. Pagan’s criminal history also includes state felony convictions for first degree assault, second degree assault, sale of narcotics, and criminal weapons possession.  It is violation of federal law for a person previously convicted of a felony offense to possess a firearm or ammunition that has moved in interstate or foreign commerce. Pagan has been detained since his arrest on related state charges on April 29, 2026.  On August 27, 2026, he pleaded guilty to unlawful possession of a firearm by a felon. Judge Dooley sentenced Pagan to 78 months of imprisonment for the firearm offense, and a consecutive 12 months of imprisonment for violating the conditions of his supervised release. This matter was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), the Connecticut State Police, and the New London Police Department.  The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Justyn P. Stokely and Jocelyn Courtney Kaoutzanis. This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. Updated November 19, 2026 Topics Operation Take Back America Firearms Offenses Component USAO - Connecticut

title: Sullivan Man Sentenced to 24 Years in Prison for Possession of 4.7 Pounds of Fentanyl and Nearly 17 Pounds of Meth
body: Press Release Sullivan Man Sentenced to 24 Years in Prison for Possession of 4.7 Pounds of Fentanyl and Nearly 17 Pounds of Meth Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Missouri SPRINGFIELD, Mo. – A Sullivan, Mo., man was sentenced in federal court yesterday for possession with the intent to distribute 4.7 pounds of fentanyl in southwest Missouri. Tyler Kittrell, 40, was sentenced before U.S. District Judge Megan Blair Benton to 292 months imprisonment   without parole, followed by five years of supervised release. Kittrell pleaded guilty on May 6, 2026, to possession with intent to distribute 400 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing a detectable amount of fentanyl. Kittrell was stopped on Interstate 44 by Joplin, Mo., police officers on Feb. 14, 2025. When officers searched Kittrell’s vehicle, they found $13,120 in cash and multiple packages containing methamphetamine and fentanyl. Officers seized approximately 16.8 pounds of methamphetamine and 4.7 pounds of fentanyl from inside the vehicle. This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Hannah R. Lucas. It was investigated by the Joplin, Mo., Police Department and the Federal Bureau of Investigation. Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Component USAO - Missouri, Western

title: Northeast Georgia Man Charged with International Money Laundering and  Destroying Evidence Tied to ISIS
body: Press Release Northeast Georgia Man Charged with International Money Laundering and  Destroying Evidence Tied to ISIS Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Northeast Georgia Man Charged with International Money Laundering and  Destroying Evidence Tied to ISIS Note : Please see the complaint here . A Lavonia, Georgia, resident is in federal custody charged by criminal complaint with international money laundering and destruction of evidence following an FBI investigation into allegations of sending more than $26,000 to individuals and groups affiliated with a designated foreign terrorist organization, the Islamic State of Iraq and al Sham (ISIS). Younes Moustafa Younes, 34, of Lavonia, Georgia, was charged by complaint with one count of international money laundering and one count of destruction of evidence. If convicted, Younes faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison, to be followed by three years of supervised release, and a $500,000 fine for international money laundering, and a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison, to be followed by three years of supervised release, and a $250,000 fine for destroying evidence. He made his initial appearance today in federal court before U.S. Magistrate Judge Charles Weigle and will remain in federal custody pending his preliminary and detention hearings on Nov. 23 in Macon. Alleged images of Younes on March 10, 2022 (top) and on May 6, 2026 (bottom) were captured by cryptocurrency ATMs According to the complaint, between December 2025 and June 2026, Younes sent $16,807 through cryptocurrency transactions using multiple phone numbers and accounts intended to conceal his identity. Investigators allege that at least some of the funds were intended to promote the efforts of ISIS in Syria. In addition, Younes is alleged to have altered and destroyed evidence up until his arrest on Nov. 18, when FBI Atlanta agents executed warrants to search his apartment, car, electronic devices, and workplace. The FBI found three cellular phones submerged in an unknown solution inside his Lavonia apartment, including one device that was smashed and another with its identification number removed. Agents also found shredded documents submerged in an unknown solution in a bathtub. Destroyed cell phones (top) in an unknown liquid solution and shredded paper (bottom) in an unknown liquid solution found in Younes’ Lavonia, Georgia, apartment on Nov. 18, 2026. The FBI first identified Younes in 2020 after he allegedly accessed ISIS propaganda online. When interviewed by law enforcement, Younes acknowledged viewing the material but denied supporting extremist ideologies. The complaint alleges that, over time, Younes became increasingly radicalized, expressing support for ISIS and other terrorist figures and organizations through encrypted communications with associates. The complaint further alleges that in 11 separate transactions between December 2021 and April 2022, Younes is alleged to have sent approximately $9,206 to cryptocurrency addresses associated with this effort, using an alias to conceal his support. Encrypted communications cited in the complaint allegedly show Younes sharing extremist content, discussing support for ISIS, and praising individuals associated with terrorist organizations. In September 2022, Younes traveled to Turkey on a one-way ticket and remained there for approximately two years after allegedly selling his vehicle, cashing out retirement funds, and leaving his employment in the United States. Following his arrest and deportation from Turkey back to the United States, investigators allege that Younes continued to express support for extremist causes and maintained contacts with individuals previously convicted on terrorism-related charges. FBI Atlanta is investigating the case, with assistance from FBI Newark and the National Counterterrorism Center. Criminal Chief Leah McEwen and Assistant U.S. Attorney Daniel Peach for the Middle District of Georgia, Assistant U.S. Attorney Sammi Malek for the District of New Jersey, and the National Security Division's Counterterrorism Section are prosecuting the case for the government. A criminal complaint is merely allegations of criminal conduct. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Updated November 19, 2026 Topic National Security Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) National Security Division (NSD) USAO - Georgia, Middle Press Release Number: 26-1384

title: Former Hacienda Employee Sentenced to 50 Months in Prison for His Participation in a Bribery Conspiracy Involving Loss of $5 Million
body: Press Release Former Hacienda Employee Sentenced to 50 Months in Prison for His Participation in a Bribery Conspiracy Involving Loss of $5 Million Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Puerto Rico SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico – On November 18, 2026, United States District Court Judge Silvia Carreño Coll sentenced former Hacienda employee Luis A. Jiménez-Guzmán to 50 months in prison, two years of supervised release, and restitution of 5 million dollars for his role in a bribery conspiracy to defraud the Puerto Rico Department of Treasury (PRDT or Hacienda), announced Héctor Ramírez Carbó, Acting United States Attorney for the District of Puerto Rico.  On July 2, 2026, Jiménez-Guzmán was charged and pleaded guilty to a bribery conspiracy involving the loss of approximately $5,000,000 in Puerto Rico tax revenue, in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 371. According to the plea agreement in the case, Luis A. Jiménez-Guzmán, knowingly and willfully conspired to commit federal program bribery and wire fraud, as well as accepted bribe payments in exchange for his corrupt acts. From February 2019 through March 2023, Jiménez-Guzmán was an employee and agent of the PRDT with duties that included physically and electronically accessing and reviewing tax returns and documents related to invoicing and collection of owed taxes. The defendant had privileged access to the PRDT’s online platforms, the Puerto Rico Integrated Tax Administration System (PRITAS) and the Internal Revenue Unified System (GenTax/SURI) and was able to access, monitor, and modify taxpayer information, including creating taxpayer credits, modifying income tax, employee retention tax and sales tax information. As part of the bribery conspiracy, Jiménez-Guzmán corruptly accepted cash payments and other benefits, in exchange for submitting false information to the PRDT. The false information was submitted to the PRDT for the elimination of taxes owed, evasion of taxes, and theft of funds. For example, on August 16, 2021, Jiménez-Guzmán received a $10,000 bribe payment from Person H to erase and reduce a tax debt of one of Person H’s customers. The illicit payments were solicited and accepted by Jiménez-Guzmán, who illegally eliminated the PRDT tax liabilities and obtained illegal tax refunds for several individual and business taxpayers, with a total approximate loss to the PRDT of $5,000,000. Acting U.S. Attorney Héctor Ramírez-Carbó of the District of Puerto Rico; and Carlos R. Goris, Special Agent in Charge of FBI San Juan Field Office made the announcement. The Federal Bureau of Investigation investigated these matters. Assistant U.S. Attorney Marie Christine Amy from the District of Puerto Rico’s Financial Fraud & Public Corruption Section prosecuted this case. This is part of an ongoing effort to combat public corruption and fraud committed by Puerto Rico Department of Treasury employees. The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Puerto Rico previously announced the indictment of twenty-six individuals and corporations in October 2025 and the guilty pleas of three Hacienda employees, Luis A. Jiménez-Guzmán , Harry E. Mueriel-Falero , and Alexander Ortiz-Robles . # # # Updated November 19, 2026 Topics Fraud Financial Fraud Public Corruption Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Puerto Rico Press Release Number: 2026-126

title: Justice Department’s Statement on the Closing of Its Investigation of NextEra’s Acquisition of Dominion
body: Press Release Justice Department’s Statement on the Closing of Its Investigation of NextEra’s Acquisition of Dominion Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs The U.S. Department of Justice issued the following statement today in connection with the closing of the Antitrust Division’s investigation into the acquisition of Dominion Energy Inc. (Dominion) by NextEra Energy Inc. (NextEra) (together, “the Parties”): The Antitrust Division continues to focus on the needs of electricity customers across the country to ensure that they benefit from competition among electricity generators. As demands on electricity grids increase, it is critical that wholesale electricity and capacity markets are competitive and cannot be exploited in a way that could leave American businesses and consumers facing higher electricity bills. The Parties’ commitment to FERC eliminating their unilateral right to deactivate units in New England will protect consumers in the region from potentially hundreds of millions of dollars of increased electricity costs. On May 18, NextEra and Dominion announced an agreement to combine the two companies in a $66.8 billion transaction. Both firms are electricity generation companies that compete in wholesale electricity and electric capacity auctions run by Regional Transmission Organizations (RTOs) or Independent System Operators (ISOs). RTOs and ISOs are nonprofit organizations responsible for managing and operating electric power grids within specific regions of the United States. These organizations rely on internal or external market monitors, who are responsible for overseeing and evaluating the electricity market’s performance. NextEra’s acquisition of Dominion combines overlapping electricity generation asset portfolios in two separate RTO/ISOs: PJM Interconnection LLC (which covers portions of the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic) and ISO New England Inc. (ISO-NE). As required by federal law, NextEra and Dominion have filed an application with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) for approval of the transaction. During FERC’s ongoing review process, the Internal Market Monitor of ISO-NE submitted comments to FERC regarding the potential impact of the transaction on the electric capacity market. Electric capacity markets ensure the availability of a reserve of capacity that an ISO or RTO can call on to provide network reliability during periods of peak electricity demand. They do this by paying generators to keep plants on-call and available to produce electricity, independent of any payments the generators receive from the sale of electricity generation. The Internal Market Monitor expressed concerns that the transaction might give the merged firm the incentive and ability to deactivate a plant that still is economically viable with the goal of using its combined portfolio to increase capacity payments in New England. To address this concern, the Internal Market Monitor proposed that the merged firm agree to allow the Internal Market Monitor to investigate any plant that the merged firm proposes to deactivate for a five-year period beginning with the next ISO-NE capacity auction in May 2028. If the Internal Market Monitor determines that the plant continues to have economic value, then NextEra would be prohibited from deactivating it. Following a detailed investigation — which included review of documents, interviews of industry participants, and sophisticated economic modeling — the Division remained concerned about the potential impact of the transaction on ISO-NE’s capacity market. After the Division informed the Parties of these concerns, the Parties told FERC in a filing on FERC’s docket that they will “commit, without qualification , to comply” with the Internal Market Monitor’s proposal regardless of whether FERC imposes it as a condition for approval of the transaction. In light of the Division’s review and the Parties’ commitment to FERC, the Antitrust Division decided that its investigation could be closed. Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Antitrust Component Antitrust Division Press Release Number: 26-1388

title: Massachusetts Maritime Academy Assistant Football Coach Arrested for Allegedly Sexually Exploiting Minors
body: Press Release Massachusetts Maritime Academy Assistant Football Coach Arrested for Allegedly Sexually Exploiting Minors Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts Defendant allegedly posed as a teenager online and solicited child sexual abuse material from at least five minors BOSTON – An assistant football coach at Massachusetts Maritime Academy was arrested today and charged with allegedly possessing child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and inducing an 11-year-old girl to produce CSAM. Garrett Luke Owens, 28, of Buzzards Bay, Mass., was charged by criminal complaint with one count of sexual exploitation of children and one count of possession of child pornography. Owens was arrested this morning and remains detained following an initial appearance today in federal court in Boston. According to the charging documents, during the investigation it was determined that Owens allegedly communicated with at least five minor victims through text messaging and social-media applications, including Snapchat and TikTok. Owens allegedly used aliases including “Garry,” “Garrison,” and “Grayson,” falsely representing himself to be a 15- or 16-year-old boy and soliciting sexually explicit images and videos from underage girls. It is alleged that the investigation began after law enforcement in Crete, Neb., reviewed the phone of a 14-year-old girl and discovered sexually explicit communications with a contact named “Garry.” The telephone number associated with the communications was allegedly linked to Owens. Records associated with Owens’ iCloud account allegedly contained child sexual abuse material involving multiple minor victims. According to the complaint, additional victims were identified in Texas, New Mexico and Maine. The victims allegedly reported that Owens initially contacted them through TikTok or other social-media platforms before moving the communications to Snapchat or text messaging. Owens allegedly continued to solicit sexually explicit material after learning that the victims were minors and, in some instances, after the victims specifically disclosed their ages. A preliminary review of Owens’ cellphone allegedly revealed sexually explicit videos involving minors stored in a hidden photo folder. Investigators also allegedly found communications with an 11-year-old girl in which Owens confirmed her age and then induced her, through an online game, to remove her clothing and expose herself on video. The charge of sexual exploitation of children provides for a mandatory minimum sentence of 15 years and up to 30 years in prison, at least five years and up to a lifetime of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. The charge of possession of child pornography provides for a sentence of up to 20 years in prison, at least five years and up to a lifetime of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes governing the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Jeff Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in New England made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the Crete (Neb.) Police Department; HSI Houston; HSI Roswell; HSI Bangor; and other federal, state and local law enforcement partners. Assistant U.S. Attorney Luke A. Goldworm, of the Major Crimes Unit and Project Safe Childhood Coordinator and Assistant U.S. Attorney Catherine Conroy of the Major Crimes Unit are prosecuting the case. This case is brought as part of Project Safe Childhood. In 2006, the Department of Justice created Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative designed to protect children from exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Department’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children, as well as identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc . The details contained in the charging document are allegations. The defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in the court of law. Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Massachusetts

title: New York City Man Pleads Guilty to Sending a White Powder Letter to the Superintendent of the Coxsackie Correctional Facility
body: Press Release New York City Man Pleads Guilty to Sending a White Powder Letter to the Superintendent of the Coxsackie Correctional Facility Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov On November 12, 2026, James McDonaugh, age 49, of Manhattan, New York, pled guilty to conveying a hoax involving a white powder letter.  First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Craig L. Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Albany Field Office for the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), made the announcement. As part of his guilty plea, McDonaugh admitted that on December 17, 2024, while serving as an inmate at the Coxsackie Correctional Facility, he used the prison’s internal mail system to send an envelope to the prison’s Superintendent.  The envelope contained a letter and some white powder.  The letter said “ANtrax DIE BITCH”. McDonaugh further admitted that he intended to scare members of the Superintendent’s staff into believing that anthrax, a dangerous biological agent, was in the envelope. McDonaugh faces up to five years of imprisonment, a $250,000 fine, and up to three years of supervised release. A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the particular statute(s) the defendant is convicted of violating, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors. Sentencing is currently scheduled for March 15, 2027, at 12:30 pm in Albany, New York, before U.S. District Judge, Elizabeth C. Coombe. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III said: “Using white powder letter hoaxes to scare members of law enforcement who are simply doing their job will not be tolerated by my office. Mr. McDonaugh’s actions have earned him some additional time behind bars.” “Mr. McDonaugh’s reckless decision to send a hoax white powder letter through the prison’s mail system just extended his stay behind bars,” said Craig Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albany Field Office. “The FBI takes hoax threats very seriously and will continue to work with our law enforcement partners to ensure anyone who tries to cause fear and chaos through these calculated actions is brought to justice. The FBI investigated the case with assistance from the New York State Department of Corrections and Community Supervision.  Assistant U.S. Attorney Rick Belliss is prosecuting the case. Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Domestic Terrorism Component USAO - New York, Northern

Federal grand jury indicts five alleged members of North Texas drug trafficking organization
body: Press Release Federal grand jury indicts five alleged members of North Texas drug trafficking organization Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas DALLAS — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that a federal grand jury has returned an indictment charging five individuals for their alleged roles in a drug trafficking conspiracy involving methamphetamine, heroin, and fentanyl in the Dallas area. Jose Mendoza, Roberto Duran, Kamerun Francis Herlehy, Julie Lynn Wilson, and Brooke Harrell are charged with conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute controlled substances. The indictment alleges that from approximately July through the beginning of October, the defendants conspired to distribute more than 500 grams of methamphetamine, more than one kilogram of heroin, and fentanyl. In addition to the conspiracy charge, Jose Mendoza is charged with possession with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of methamphetamine and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. The indictment alleges that Mendoza possessed a Ruger LCP semi-automatic handgun in furtherance of his drug trafficking activities on or about October 1. Kamerun Francis Herlehy is also charged with possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. According to the indictment, Herlehy possessed a Sig Sauer P938 pistol in furtherance of the charged drug trafficking conspiracy on or about August 20. “The distribution of methamphetamine, heroin, and fentanyl threatens the safety and well-being of our communities,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “This case represents the successful dismantling of a large-scale drug trafficking organization responsible for flooding Dallas-area streets with deadly narcotics. Through the coordinated efforts of our federal, state, and local law enforcement partners, we disrupted a network that profited from addiction and fueled violence throughout our communities. We will continue to aggressively pursue those who traffic these dangerous substances and hold them accountable.” “This investigation targeted a criminal organization that was trafficking large quantities of methamphetamine, heroin and fentanyl, all while using firearms in furtherance of this criminal operation,” said DEA Dallas Field Division Special Agent in Charge Joseph B. Tucker. “We will continue to work with our federal, state, and local partners, to identify, disrupt, and dismantle these networks to protect our communities and hold accountable those who prioritize profit over law.” The indictment includes forfeiture allegations seeking approximately $59,033 in U.S. currency and multiple firearms allegedly used in connection with the charged offenses, including the Ruger and Sig Sauer pistols identified in the indictment. If convicted, Mendoza, Duran, and Herlehy face substantial prison terms . The drug conspiracy charge carries a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years in federal prison and a maximum sentence of life imprisonment, with enhanced penalties potentially applicable to certain defendants based on prior felony drug convictions. The firearm charges carry mandatory consecutive prison sentences. The Drug Enforcement Administration Dallas Division, Texas Department of Public Safety, and the Dallas Police Department conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Abby Policastro from the Cartel and National Security Section is prosecuting the case. An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Contact Public Affairs Division U.S. Attorney’s Office Northern District of Texas USATXN.Media@usdoj.gov Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Component USAO - Texas, Northern

title: Waterbury Man Admits Role in Mail Theft Scheme
body: Press Release Waterbury Man Admits Role in Mail Theft Scheme Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Connecticut David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, and Justin Page, Acting Inspector in Charge of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Boston Division, announced that MARCUS ANTHONY SIMMS, 28, of Waterbury, waived his right to be indicted and pleaded guilty today before U.S. District Judge Omar A. Williams in Hartford to conspiracy to steal U.S. mail. According to court documents and statements made in court, early in the morning on May 26, 2025, Simms drove with two associates to the Milford Post Office on Pepes Farm Road in Milford.  While Simms remained inside the vehicle, his associates exited the vehicle and attempted to pry open a large U.S. Postal Service collection box using a screwdriver and other tools.  The co-conspirators damaged the collection box, particularly the locking mechanism, but were unable to open it.  The screwdriver was left at the scene. Simms was arrested on November 7, 2025. At sentencing, which is not scheduled, Simms faces a maximum term of imprisonment of five years.  He also has agreed to pay $4,139 in restitution to the USPS. Simms is released on a $100,000 bond pending sentencing, This matter has been investigated by the U.S. Postal Inspection Service and the Milford Police Department.  The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Hal Chen. Updated November 19, 2026 Component USAO - Connecticut

title: Two Illegal Aliens Plead Guilty to Smuggling Illegal Aliens Into the United States
body: Press Release Two Illegal Aliens Plead Guilty to Smuggling Illegal Aliens Into the United States Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nevada RENO – A father and son, both illegal aliens from Mexico, each pleaded guilty to their roles in a human smuggling operation that brought in and harbored illegal aliens in the Reno area for financial gain. “These defendants prioritized illicit profit over human life and the rule of law, operating a family-run smuggling enterprise that endangered both the individuals they transported and the communities along our border,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “Working alongside our federal and local law enforcement partners, our office remains committed to dismantling human smuggling networks at every level and holding those who exploit our nation’s immigration laws fully accountable.” “Human smugglers who exploit vulnerable people through coercion, threats and demands for payment will be pursued and held accountable,” said Jonathan Sherwin, Deputy Special Agent in Charge for HSI Las Vegas. “HSI and our law enforcement partners will continue to dismantle the networks that profit from smuggling and harboring illegal aliens, while protecting those subjected to exploitation and abuse.” According to court documents and statements made in court, from November 1, 2024, and continuing up to March 11, 2025, Carlos Recinos-Valdez aided another person with bringing more than six but less than 25 illegal aliens into the United States. The illegal aliens were detained through coercion or threat or in connection with a demand for payment after the alien was smuggled into the United States or while the alien was transported or harbored in the United States. On March 13, 2023, and continuing up to March 11, 2025, Recinos-Valdez’s son Kevin Recinos-Ruano conspired with others to harbor illegal aliens in buildings in and around Reno and transporting illegal aliens between the buildings. The buildings where the illegal aliens were harbored were controlled and paid for by other members of the conspiracy to hide the aliens from law enforcement. Recinos-Ruano pleaded guilty today to one count of conspiracy to harbor illegal aliens. He faces a maximum statutory penalty of five years in prison. Sentencing is scheduled for December 2, 2026. Recinos-Valdez pleaded guilty on November 17, 2026, to one count of aiding and abetting bringing illegal aliens into the United States. He faces a maximum statutory penalty of 10 years in prison with a minimum statutory penalty of three years in prison. Sentencing is scheduled for February 16, 2027. HSI investigated the case with significant assistance from the Reno Police Department, the Sparks Police Department, the Douglas County Sheriff’s Office, and the Washoe County Sheriff’s Office. Assistant United States Attorney Clay Plummer is prosecuting the case. You can report suspicious criminal activity to the ICE Tip Line 24 hours a day, seven days a week by calling 866-DHS-2-ICE (866-347-2423) or online at https://www.ice.gov/webform/ice-tip-form . ### Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Human Smuggling Component USAO - Nevada

title: Convicted Murderer Sentenced to More Than 20 Years for Armed Carjacking and Witness Tampering
body: Press Release Convicted Murderer Sentenced to More Than 20 Years for Armed Carjacking and Witness Tampering Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Oklahoma TULSA, Okla. – U.S. District Judge Sara E. Hill sentenced Christopher Ray Barrett, 41, to 246 months in federal prison for carjacking, brandishing a firearm during a crime of violence, possessing a firearm and ammunition as a convicted felon, and conspiring to tamper with witnesses. Barrett pleaded guilty to the charges in November 2025. According to court documents, Barrett, who goes by the alias “SloMo,” forcibly took a victim’s 2012 Volkswagen Passat at gunpoint on Dec. 29, 2024. After the victim drove an acquaintance to a Tulsa residence, Barrett entered the vehicle, pressed a revolver against the victim’s head, and demanded information about property inside the car. Barrett then forced the victim to unload the vehicle, confiscated the victim’s keys and cellphone, and threatened multiple individuals at the residence with the revolver. Court records show Barrett held the victim at gunpoint inside the residence for approximately one hour, before forcibly abducting the victim to retrieve the Passat’s title from the victim’s home. Days later, Tulsa Police officers located Barrett driving the stolen Passat and recovered a loaded Smith & Wesson .38-caliber revolver from inside the vehicle. Law enforcement’s continued investigation revealed that, following his arrest, Barrett conspired with others to locate and threaten  witnesses to the carjacking in an effort to prevent their testimony in the federal case. Barrett directed the witness tampering conspiracy while incarcerated pending trial. According to sentencing records, Barrett committed these offenses only months after being released from a twenty-year state prison sentence. Additionally, Oklahoma state courts had previously imposed six lifetime suspended sentences. Barrett’s criminal history includes convictions for second-degree murder, assault with a dangerous weapon, felon in possession of a firearm, and multiple vehicle theft-related crimes. The Court found that Barrett’s extensive history of violent criminal  and continued criminal conduct warranted a substantial federal sentence. Two additional defendants were prosecuted for their participation in the witness-tampering conspiracy and have also been sentenced. The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives and the Tulsa Police Department investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Mike Flesher and Jessica Wright prosecuted the case. Updated November 19, 2026 Component USAO - Oklahoma, Northern

Two Mexican nationals indicted for methamphetamine trafficking
body: Press Release Two Mexican nationals indicted for methamphetamine trafficking Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of California SACRAMENTO, Calif. — A federal grand jury returned a two-count indictment today against Yair Contreras Gomez, 22, a Mexican national residing in Portland, Oregon, and Pablo Lopez Morales, 29, a Mexican national residing in Sacramento, California, charging them with conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine and charging Contreras Gomez with possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced. According to court documents, on multiple occasions between July 29, 2026, and Aug. 31, 2026, Contreras Gomez directed Lopez Morales to bring loads of methamphetamine from southern California to Portland. On Aug. 31, law enforcement officers intercepted one of these loads during a traffic stop while Lopez Morales was traveling northbound on Interstate 5 through Shasta County. The officers seized approximately 30 pounds of methamphetamine from inside the door panels of the vehicle. The Drug Enforcement Administration conducted the investigation with assistance from Homeland Security Investigations and the California Highway Patrol. Assistant U.S. Attorney David W. Spencer is prosecuting the case. If convicted, the defendants face a mandatory minimum of 10 years in prison, a maximum statutory penalty of life in prison, and a $10 million fine. Any sentence, however, would be determined at the discretion of the court after consideration of any applicable statutory factors and the federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account a number of variables. The charges are only allegations; the defendant is presumed innocent until and unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Sacramento is composed of agents and officers from Homeland Security Investigations, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Drug Enforcement Administration, Northern California High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area, Central Valley High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area, and the Sacramento County Sheriff’s Office with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of California. Updated November 19, 2026 Topics Homeland Security Task Force Drug Trafficking Component USAO - California, Eastern

title: Registered Sex Offender Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison for Possession of Child Pornography
body: Press Release Registered Sex Offender Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison for Possession of Child Pornography Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts Defendant was on state probation for possession of child pornography at the time of offense BOSTON – A registered sex offender from Holyoke has been sentenced in federal court in Springfield, Mass. for possessing child pornography. Justin Ouimette, 35, was sentenced on Nov. 17, 2026 by U.S. District Court Judge Mark Mastroianni to 10 years in prison, to be followed by 15 years of supervised release. In August 2026 , Ouimette pleaded guilty to possession of child pornography. Ouimette was charged by complaint in May 2025 and has remained in custody since that time. Ouimette was identified as the owner of a Dropbox account uploading child sexual abuse material (CSAM). During the search of Ouimette’s residence, an electronic device was found to contain hundreds of files of CSAM depicting children as young as toddlers. Subsequent searches of Ouimette’s cloud storage accounts revealed hundreds of additional files depicting CSAM. Ouimette was previously convicted in Massachusetts Superior Court of possession of child pornography in October 2022 and was on state probation when he committed this new offense. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Boston Division made the announcement today. Assistant U.S. Attorney Caroline Merck of the Springfield Office prosecuted the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse, launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the DOJ’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children, as well as identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Massachusetts

title: Buffalo woman arrested, charged with possession of large quantities of fentanyl and cocaine following Homeland Security Task Force investigation
body: Press Release Buffalo woman arrested, charged with possession of large quantities of fentanyl and cocaine following Homeland Security Task Force investigation Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of New York BUFFALO, N.Y. - U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Keionna Goins, 48, of Buffalo, NY, was arrested and charged by criminal complaint with possession with intent to distribute a large quantity of fentanyl and cocaine, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison, and a $1,000,000 fine. According to the criminal complaint, on November 17, 2026, the Homeland Security Task Force and Buffalo Police executed a search warrant at a Comstock Avenue residence. Goins, the lone occupant in the residence, was encountered at the front door of the residence, handcuffed and taken into custody. During the search of the residence, investigators seized approximately 10,166 grams of suspected fentanyl, and 2,697 grams of suspected cocaine. They also recovered a large quantity of suspected methamphetamine, approximately 633 grams of suspected MDMA, a large amount of cash, and a loaded .38 caliber revolver. “This case goes to the heart of the mission of the Homeland Security Task Force,” stated U.S. Attorney DiGiacomo. “Law enforcement at all levels working together to remove literally hundreds of thousands of dollars’ worth of dangerous narcotics from the streets of Buffalo, the type of narcotics trafficking that often results in violence in our community. The Buffalo Homeland Security Task Force is tops in removing drugs and bringing to justice the criminals that peddle them.” HSI Special Agent-in-Charge Anthony Patrone stated, “Every day, we see the scourges of fentanyl leave a lasting, costly impact on our neighborhoods — it poisons our communities, fuels violence and endangers the vulnerable. The progress announced today puts those who profit from harm on notice: if you exploit our communities to move dangerous contraband that victimizes members of our communities, you will face a coordinated law enforcement response. HSI Buffalo and our HSTF partners will continue to work across agencies to disrupt criminal networks, protect the public, and strengthen the security of the communities we serve.” Goins made an initial appearance before U.S. Magistrate Judge Jeremiah J. McCarthy and was held pending a detention hearing on November 20, 2026. This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Buffalo comprises agents and officers from Homeland Security Investigations, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigations, Department of Homeland Security Enforcement and Removal Operations, Customs and Border Protection, the Drug Enforcement Administration, the U.S. Coast Guard Investigative Service, the U.S. Marshals Service, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, the U.S. Secret Service, and the Diplomatic Security Service, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of New York. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney MacCaelin Sedita. The complaint is the result of an investigation by Homeland Security Investigations, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Anthony Patrone, the Buffalo Police Department, under the direction of Chief Erika Shields, and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, firearms, and Explosives, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Bryan DiGirolamo, New York Field Division. The fact that a defendant has been charged with a crime is merely an accusation and the defendant is presumed innocent until and unless proven guilty. # # # # Contact Barbara Burns 716-843-5817 Updated November 19, 2026 Topics Homeland Security Task Force Drug Trafficking Opioids Component USAO - New York, Western

Columbia Man Pleads Guilty to Being a Felon in Possession of a Firearm
body: Press Release Columbia Man Pleads Guilty to Being a Felon in Possession of a Firearm Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of South Carolina COLUMBIA, S.C. — Kyreem Dreveon Tindal, 24, of Columbia, has pleaded guilty to being a felon in possession of a firearm. On Aug. 1, 2023, Columbia Police Department conducted a lawful traffic stop of a vehicle in downtown Columbia after learning that the driver, who was driving under suspension, was live streaming from the vehicle with a passenger who had a firearm sitting in his lap. The passenger, Tindal, ran from the vehicle. Officers found Tindal hiding in nearby bushes and recovered the firearm Tindal dropped while running. The firearm had previously been reported stolen in Charlotte, N.C. DNA analysis of the firearm linked it to Tindal. Tindal has prior state convictions for assault and battery 1st degree and discharging a firearm into a dwelling. Tindal participated in the Ceasefire program hosted by the City of Columbia Police Department. The Ceasefire program identifies offenders who are at risk of future firearms offenses and introduces them to community resources such as substance abuse treatment and employment services. During participation in the program, law enforcement emphasizes the likelihood of future state and federal prosecution if participants, like Tindal, reoffend. Following his participation, Tindal was charged with an unrelated state offense, leading to the federal prosecution of the 2023 gun offense. Tindal faces a maximum penalty of 15 years in federal prison. He also faces a fine of up to $250,000, restitution, and three of supervision to follow the term of imprisonment.  United States District Judge Mary Geiger Lewis accepted the guilty plea and will sentence Tindal after receiving and reviewing a sentencing report prepared by the U.S. Probation Office. Tindal remains in custody awaiting sentencing. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. This case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Firearms, Tobacco and Explosives and the Columbia Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Stacey D. Haynes is prosecuting the case. ### Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Project Safe Neighborhoods Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - South Carolina

title: Ecuadorian National Pleads Guilty to Committing Several Truck Thefts, Including Stealing $100 Million in Jewelry from Brinks Truck
body: Press Release Ecuadorian National Pleads Guilty to Committing Several Truck Thefts, Including Stealing $100 Million in Jewelry from Brinks Truck Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Central District of California RIVERSIDE, California – An Ecuadorian national pleaded guilty today to committing several thefts, including a July 2022 heist in which approximately $100 million worth of jewelry was stolen from a Brinks semitruck stopped in the Central Valley while it was en route from an international jewelry show in Northern California. Carlos Victor Mestanza Cercado, 33, whose previous addresses include one in Pasadena and who is the lead defendant in this case, pleaded guilty to one count of interference with commerce by robbery (Hobbs Act). Mestanza has been in federal custody since August 2025 after being extradited from Panama, where he had fled upon learning of the criminal charges in this case. According to his plea agreement, from March 2022 to July 2022, Mestanza and other co-conspirators used multiple vehicles to follow truck drivers carrying interstate and foreign shipments to stopping points, including truck stops and other locations where the drivers stopped and their trucks were left unattended. Mestanza and his accomplices then stole the cargo, including by force and threat of force in the presence of the victims. The thieves then returned to Los Angeles County with the stolen merchandise to divide up and sell for profit. In July 2022, a co-conspirator scouted an international jewelry show in San Mateo, communicating by phone with Mestanza and other co-conspirators to steal the jewelry in transit following the show. On July 10, 2022, Mestanza and co-conspirators focused on a Brinks semitruck at the jewelry show that carried 73 bags containing millions of dollars’ worth of jewelry that had traveled in interstate commerce. When the Brinks truck departed, Mestanza and the co-conspirators coordinated by phone and, from the late evening of July 10, 2022, to the early morning of July 11, 2022, followed the truck approximately 300 miles from San Mateo to rest stops in the Central Valley. On July 11, 2022, at a truck stop in Lebec, Mestanza and his accomplices broke the locks on the Brinks truck and stole 24 bags of jewelry, which the victims later valued at approximately $100 million. They then traveled to East Hollywood with the stolen jewelry. In the days that followed, Mestanza and other co-conspirators tried to conceal their identities by deactivating the cellphone numbers they had used to steal the jewelry from the Brinks truck. Mestanza fled the U.S. in June 2025 after a federal grand jury indicted him and several other defendants in connection with the Brinks theft. On July 1, 2025, law enforcement detained Mestanza at Tocumen International Airport in Panama City during a layover from Guatemala to Ecuador. Mestanza further admitted to committing several other thefts with co-conspirators. Specifically, on March 2, 2022, they stole Samsung electronics from a truck at a 7-Eleven store in Ontario, making off with approximately $240,573 in stolen goods that were brought to a co-conspirator’s residence in Los Angeles. On March 11, 2022, Mestanza and others stole Apple AirTags that had traveled from China and were being delivered by truck to a warehouse in Fontana. The truck’s driver had stopped for food when the robbery occurred, and a co-conspirator used a knife to threaten the driver. The thieves made off with approximately $57,377 in stolen goods. Finally, on May 25, 2022, Mestanza and others broke into one truck and stole items from another truck parked at stops in Fontana, stealing approximately $14,081 worth of Samsung electronics. Law enforcement believes that the applicable amount of restitution in this case is at least $100,312,031. United States District Judge Kenly Kiya Kato scheduled an April 15, 2027 sentencing hearing, at which time Mestanza will face a statutory maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison. The following defendants charged in this case have pleaded not guilty and are scheduled to go on trial on March 22, 2027: Alberto Javier Loza, 40, a.k.a. “Ricardo Noel Moya, “Ricardo Barbosa,” “Alberto Javier Loza Chamorro,” and “Jazael Padilla Resto,” of Boyle Heights, who is a citizen of Ecuador; Pablo Raul Lugo Larroig, 43, a.k.a. “Walter Loza,” of Rialto, who is a U.S. citizen; and Jorge Enrique Alban, 34, of South Los Angeles, who also is a U.S. citizen. Co-defendants Victor Hugo Valencia Solorzano and Eduardo Macias Ibarra have not appeared in a U.S. courtroom to face the criminal charges against them. On February 12, the charges against Jeson Nelon Presilla Flores, 44, formerly of Upland, were dismissed without prejudice. Presilla, a citizen of Ecuador, has been removed from the United States. The FBI, the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, the Fontana Police Department, and the Ontario Police Department are investigating this matter. Assistant United States Attorneys Jena A. MacCabe and Kevin J. Butler of the Major Crimes Section are prosecuting this case. Contact Shawn Lewis Public Affairs Officer shawn.lewis@usdoj.gov (213) 458-6803 Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Violent Crime Component USAO - California, Central Press Release Number: 26-222

Kansas Realtor Indicted for Tax Evasion, Failure to File Tax Returns, and Pandemic Relief Fraud
body: Press Release Kansas Realtor Indicted for Tax Evasion, Failure to File Tax Returns, and Pandemic Relief Fraud Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs A federal grand jury in Kansas City, Kansas, returned a superseding indictment yesterday charging a Louisburg, Kansas, woman with tax evasion, wire fraud, and willful failure to file personal and corporate income tax returns. According to the superseding indictment, Michelle O’Connor, also known as Michelle Yi Lee, owned and operated a realty company based in the Kansas City metro area. For the years 2008 through 2015, O’Connor allegedly filed federal income tax returns, self-reporting that she owed a total of approximately $300,000 in taxes. According to the superseding indictment, despite reporting to the IRS that she owed taxes, O’Connor did not pay the amounts owed. Starting in 2010, the IRS allegedly began trying to collect the outstanding taxes from O’Connor and sent her a total of more than 50 notices. From 2011 through late 2020, however, O’Connor allegedly stymied the IRS’s collections efforts by, among other things, filing false or frivolous bankruptcy petitions and reducing her bank balances by purchasing more than $250,000 in cashier’s checks to prevent the IRS from levying those accounts. According to the superseding indictment, O’Connor closed some of her personal bank accounts and maintained minimal balances in others in an effort to further obstruct the IRS’s collection efforts. O’Connor also allegedly paid for personal expenses using her business’s bank accounts. By 2020, O’Connor allegedly owed the IRS nearly half a million in taxes, penalties and interest. In 2020, O’Connor also allegedly submitted 34 fraudulent Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) applications on behalf of her real estate business and seven other corporate entities she created for the purpose of applying for these credits. Under the EIDL program, a small business could receive a loan of up to $150,000 from the Small Business Administration to cover six months of working capital. In total, O’Connor allegedly received nearly $300,000 from her fraudulent EIDLs, which she used for personal purposes, including purchasing $115,000 of cryptocurrency. According to the superseding indictment, O’Connor also did not file individual and corporate income tax returns for the years 2020 through 2025 as required by law. O’Connor was charged with one count of tax evasion, two counts of wire fraud, five counts of willful failure to file an individual tax return, and nine counts of willful failure to file a corporate tax return. If convicted, she faces maximum penalties of five years in prison for the tax evasion count, 20 years in prison for each count of wire fraud, and one year in prison for each count of willful failure to file a tax return. She also faces a period of supervised release, restitution and monetary penalties. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser for the District of Kansas made the announcement. IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case. Trial Attorneys Dominick Giovanniello and J. Parker Gochenour of the Fraud Division’s Tax Section are prosecuting the case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. An indictment is merely an allegation and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Fraud Component National Fraud Enforcement Division Press Release Number: 26-1385

title: Sacramento man sentenced to 27 years in prison for sexually exploiting a child over Snapchat and Instagram
body: Press Release Sacramento man sentenced to 27 years in prison for sexually exploiting a child over Snapchat and Instagram Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of California SACRAMENTO, Calif. — Francisco Mariano Orantes, 33, of Sacramento, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge Daniel J. Calabretta to 27 years in prison for sexually exploiting a minor, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced. “For years, this defendant exploited children by gaining their trust through lies and then using coercion and threats to deepen their victimization,” said U.S. Attorney Grant. “Today's sentence reflects the extraordinary harm he inflicted on vulnerable young victims and ensures he will be held accountable for his crimes. The U.S. Attorney's Office remains committed to protecting children from online predators and pursuing redress for victims of exploitation and sextortion.” “There is nothing more important than protecting our children,” said Jim Cooper, Sacramento County Sheriff. “This case highlights countless hours of investigative work by our Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Detectives and law enforcement partners. I could not be more proud of them for hunting down this predator and bringing him to justice.” According to court documents, between 2023 and 2024, Orantes persuaded or coerced at least seven minor female victims to produce sexually explicit images and videos. Using apps like Snapchat and Instagram, Orantes gained his victims’ trust by impersonating a teenage girl and convinced them to trade content. Often, he sent his victims sexually explicit images or videos of the girl he was impersonating and convinced them to produce similar imagery or videos. When his victims would replicate, Orantes would screen record his conversations and download and store the content on his devices. He categorized the images and videos by the child’s name, age or other identifier, in a folder called “Children.” Orantes pleaded guilty on May 21, 2026. One victim told law enforcement that she was coerced into sending Orantes additional material because he found out where she went to school and threatened to tell everyone at school if she did not perform as instructed. In fact, law enforcement later recovered screen recordings showing Orantes using geolocation tools to identify that minor’s address and school, and a saved text file in which he threatened to share the minor’s nude images with people at her school. Another victim similarly reported that Orantes knew her full name and address and threatened to leak her images if she did not comply with his instructions. In total, Orantes was found in possession of more than 11,000 images and more than 14,000 videos of child sexual abuse material on his devices, including images and videos showing the sexual abuse of infants or toddlers. The Internet Crimes Against Children Unit of the Sacramento Valley Hi-Tech Crimes Task Force and the Sacramento County Sheriff’s Office conducted the investigation with assistance from the Federal Bureau of Investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Dhruv M. Sharma prosecuted the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the United States Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute those who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC . Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - California, Eastern

title: Shiprock Man Charged with Assault Following Stabbing
body: Press Release Shiprock Man Charged with Assault Following Stabbing Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Mexico ALBUQUERQUE – A Shiprock man is facing federal charges for allegedly attacking a man with a utility knife at a gas station. According to court documents, on November 11, 2026, Irick Abe Phillips , 49, an enrolled member of the Navajo Nation, allegedly stabbed a man during an altercation at a gas station in Shiprock, New Mexico. The victim, an employee of the gas station, had asked Phillips to leave the premises when Phillips allegedly threatened him with a utility knife and cut him on the wrist. The victim received treatment at the scene for a laceration to his arm. Court documents allege that after the stabbing, Phillips continued to threaten the victim and attempted to follow him into the gas station while still armed with the knife. Employees locked the doors to prevent Phillips from entering. Phillips was eventually disarmed and detained by the victim and bystanders until law enforcement arrived. Law enforcement officers recovered a knife believed to have been used in the assault. Investigators also reviewed surveillance footage that corroborated witness accounts of the incident. Phillips is charged with assault with a dangerous weapon. He will remain in custody pending  trial, which has not been scheduled. If convicted of the current charge, Phillips faces up to 10 years in prison. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison and Special Agent in Charge Justin A. Garris of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office made the announcement today. The Farmington Resident Agency of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office investigated this case with assistance from the Navajo Nation Police Department and Navajo Nation Department of Criminal Investigations. Assistant U.S. Attorney Jack Burkhead is prosecuting the case. A criminal complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. title: Illegal Alien Pleads Guilty to Unlawful Reentry
body: Press Release Illegal Alien Pleads Guilty to Unlawful Reentry Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts BOSTON – A Brazilian national who recently completed a two-year sentence in the Middlesex House of Correction for Operating Under the Influence (4th or greater offense) pleaded guilty yesterday in federal court in Boston to unlawfully reentering the United States after deportation. Jose Antonio Ramos, 52, pleaded guilty to one count of unlawful reentry of a deported alien before U.S. Senior District Court Judge F. Dennis Saylor IV who scheduled sentencing for Feb. 17, 2027. Ramos was indicted by a federal grand jury in April 2026 . According to the charging documents, the defendant was removed from the United States on two occasions, once in 2006 and a second time in November 2008. After each removal, he reentered the United States at unknown dates and unknown places without being inspected or admitted by an immigration officer. The charge of unlawful reentry of a deported alien provides for a sentence of up to 10 years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. The defendant is subject to deportation upon completion of any sentence imposed. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and David T. Wesling, Acting Field Office Director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Enforcement and Removal Operations in Boston made the announcement. Assistant U.S. Attorney Suzanne Sullivan Jacobus of the Major Crimes Unit is prosecuting the case. Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Immigration Component USAO - Massachusetts
